# Cap the recovery retry-loop backoff at 10 minutes for all retry-path failures

Discovered from: WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W

## Problem statement

The recovery retry loop (`triggerInvisibleContinue` in `register-recovery.ts`)
currently caps every backoff interval at `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG.maxDelayMs =
60000` (60s) in `retry-logic.ts`. For long-lived outages — for example the
llm-proxy provider quiet-hours window ("scheduled time window") that can last
hours — the loop keeps retrying roughly once a minute indefinitely. That is
wasteful (constant churn against the proxy and the agent) and does not reflect
that the outage is long. Raise the ceiling to **10 minutes (600000 ms)** so the
backoff can settle at up to one attempt per 10 minutes for **every** failure
that takes this route.

**User story:** As an operator/unattended agent, when a retryable outage lasts
longer than a few minutes, I want the recovery loop to keep retrying
automatically but with a backoff ceiling of 10 minutes, so retries do not
hammer the provider at a fixed 60s cadence for hours.

## Current state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`:
  `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG = { baseDelayMs: 2000, maxDelayMs: 60000,
  multiplier: 2, serverHintJitterRatio: 0.25 }`.
- `register-recovery.ts` (`triggerInvisibleContinue`) calls
  `resolveRetryDelay(attempt, lastErrorMessageFromAgentState(),
  DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG, Math.random, _lastServerRetryHintMs)` — so this single
  config governs **all** retryable-path failures: SERVER_ERROR, TIMEOUT, and
  the shared loop used by CONTEXT_LENGTH and COMPACTION_GATE recovery.
- `error-patterns.ts` `DEFAULT_RECOVERY_CONFIG.<category>.maxDelayMs` mirrors
  60000 for `serverError` and `timeout`; these are the settings surface, not the
  loop's actual cap.
- `calculateDelay()` caps both the local exponential and the server-hint
  (`Retry-After`) derived delay at `maxDelayMs`.
- Tests that will need updating: `retry-after-header.test.ts` (~line 118 asserts
  a 90_000 hint is clamped to the 60s default), `retry-after.test.ts`,
  `retry-loop.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG.maxDelayMs` is `600000` (10 minutes); the constant
      is documented as the retry-loop ceiling.
- [ ] The shared retry loop reaches a 600000ms cap for high attempt numbers
      (e.g. attempt 10) across all categories that route through
      `triggerInvisibleContinue` — asserted via `calculateDelay` /
      `resolveRetryDelay`.
- [ ] A server `Retry-After` hint between 60s and 10m is honoured up to the
      600000ms cap (no longer clamped to 60000); a hint above 10m is clamped to
      600000.
- [ ] `DEFAULT_RECOVERY_CONFIG.<category>.maxDelayMs` values are made consistent
      with the new ceiling where they mirror it (`serverError`, `timeout`), or a
      comment explains why they differ.
- [ ] No regression: existing retry-after/retry-loop/retry-command/recovery
      tests pass with the updated expectations.
- [ ] Documentation/comments updated (`retry-logic.ts` and any related docs)
      describing the 10-minute ceiling.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Behaviour change only to the backoff ceiling; do **not** change base delay
  (2000ms), multiplier (2), or jitter.
- Keep the loop's single-layer design; no new dependencies.
- Closely related to `WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` ("honour long server Retry-After
  hints, do not clamp to 60s"). Raising the cap to 10m partially addresses that;
  this item must state the interaction and not duplicate it. A hint longer than
  10m remains clamped by design (10m is the requested ceiling).
- Respect the user-abort (ESC) and session-switch guards — unchanged.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — raise
  `DEFAULT_BACKOFF_CONFIG.maxDelayMs`; update docs/comments.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — align
  per-category `maxDelayMs` (or document the intentional difference).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after-header.test.ts`,
  `retry-after.test.ts`, `retry-loop.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts` — update/add
  cap assertions.

## Related work

- `WL-0MU56ZSSB0054D8W` (discovered-from) — classified the proxy scheduled-window
  503 as SERVER_ERROR; that retry path is the motivating case.
- `WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM` — honour long server Retry-After hints (do not clamp to
  60s); adjacent, overlapping on the clamp behaviour.
- `WL-0MUQO8AEE003G1Z2`, `WL-0MT656GDS0052FTK` — earlier work routing more errors
  into this retry path.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** 10 minutes is an acceptable maximum wait (operators accept up
  to 10m between automatic attempts in exchange for far less churn).
- **Risk:** raising the cap delays recovery for outages that resolve shortly
  after a long backoff; mitigated because the exponential ramp only reaches 10m
  after several attempts (2s, 4s, 8s, ... 10m).
- **Risk:** test expectations for the 60s clamp are updated in behaviour, not
  silently weakened.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **WL-0MUQO8AEE003G1Z2** – Retry proxy finish_reason error in recovery (completed)

# Prevent tests posting a real Discord release notification (Release v9.9.9)

## Problem statement

Running the release test harness posts a real notification to the configured
Discord webhook, titled `Release v9.9.9`. The side effect is harmless (no data
loss, no production impact) but noisy: the message lands in a real release
channel on every test run, and tests must never perform real outbound
notifications.

## Users

- **Developer / operator running the full test suite** — should not see
  unexpected Discord noise when testing.
  - *As a developer, when I run the release tests, no message should be posted
    to the real Discord release channel.*
- **CI operator** — test runs must be deterministic and side-effect free.
  - *As a CI operator, a test run must not depend on, or mutate, any external
    service.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No real notification.** Running the identified release test harness
   produces **no outbound HTTP request to any real Discord webhook**. Verified
   by a test that fails if the real webhook would be resolved/called during the
   harness (or by asserting the notifier is stubbed and the global-config
   fallback is unreachable in the harness).
2. **Coverage retained.** The Step 8.5 notification wiring keeps test coverage
   through a mocked/stubbed notifier (the existing
   `test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` pattern), so silencing the real send
   does not drop coverage.
3. **Regression guard.** The release integration harness cannot accidentally
   reach the real `discord-notify.js`/global webhook again — the harness injects
   a stub notifier (or an isolated global-config path/HOME), and a test pins
   this so a future copy of the real module cannot re-introduce the side effect.
4. **Testing/validation.** At least one test asserts the "no real Discord
   request" property described in AC1; the full project test suite is exercised
   locally to confirm no external notification is emitted.
5. **Docs updated.** The test-isolation rule ("tests never perform real release
   notifications") is documented in the relevant test/README or ship-skill
   reference; all related documentation, code comments, README, and any
   relevant wiki/docs-site entries are updated.
6. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Production behaviour unchanged.** Real releases must still post the Discord
  notification; only test runs must be silenced.
- **Fix at the harness boundary.** Prefer stubbing the notifier module or
  isolating the global config inside the test harness, consistent with the
  existing `test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` pattern, over changing
  production notification logic.
- **No secrets, no global mutation.** Do not commit any webhook token and do
  not mutate the operator's real `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`; isolate per test
  process if the config path is redirected.
- **Minimal, targeted change.** Do not remove or weaken unrelated release tests.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` resolves the webhook via
  `resolveDiscordWebhookUrl()` in three layers: project
  `.worklog/config.private.yaml` → project `.worklog/config.yaml` → global
  `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`. The first hit wins; if none is set the
  notification is skipped.
- `run-release.js` calls `sendReleaseNotification({ version, prUrl, projectRoot })`
  at Step 8.5. The version comes from `git describe --tags --abbrev=0`.
- The offender is `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs` (shared ship
  skill test suite): it copies the **real** `discord-notify.js` into a temp
  skill layout and runs the **real** `run-release.js` with mocked `git`/`wl`/`gh`
  binaries. The mocked `git describe` returns `v9.9.9`, and the temp project
  root has no `.worklog/` config — so webhook resolution falls back to the
  operator's global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` and a real embed titled
  `Release v9.9.9` is POSTed. The process env (including `HOME`) is inherited,
  which is why the global fallback is reachable.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` already replaces
  `discord-notify.js` with a recording stub and therefore does **not** send —
  this is the pattern to reuse.
- The ship skill's own `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` injects
  `fetchFn` for every `sendReleaseNotification` call, so it does not send.

## Desired change

1. **Remove the offending test code** that causes the real Discord
   notification in the release integration harness: in
   `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`, stop copying/executing the
   real `discord-notify.js` (remove that part of the test) so the test no
   longer performs a real notification.
2. Keep the harness's actual purpose intact — the Step 8 merge-verification
   guard and the work-item close behaviour must still be covered and green.
3. Add a regression-guard assertion that the harness cannot reach the real
   notifier / global webhook, if a simple guard is warranted.
4. Keep (or rely on the existing `test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs`)
   coverage that Step 8.5 is invoked with the resolved `projectRoot`, version,
   and PR URL.
5. Document the "tests never post real release notifications" rule.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs` — The offender: copies the real
  `discord-notify.js` and inherits `HOME`; needs a stubbed notifier (or an
  isolated global-config path) so Step 8.5 cannot send.
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs` — Reference pattern: already
  substitutes a mock notifier that records arguments; reuse this harness shape.
- `skill/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — Optional test-only guard (e.g. a
  `DISABLE_DISCORD_NOTIFY`/test-env short-circuit) **only** if harness-level
  stubbing is insufficient; production behaviour must be unchanged.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_discord_notify.mjs` — Confirm coverage of
  `sendReleaseNotification` remains intact after the change.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and/or the test suite README —
  Document the test-isolation rule.

## Related work

- **WL-0MN1X7DIT0UVXTC8** — Remove TUI browser-opening test (completed). Same
  class of defect: a test performing a real external side effect. Its approach
  (mock the boundary or add a test-only guard; do not change production
  behaviour) is the precedent to follow.
- **WL-0MUWEPN6X0044R43** — Consume the project CTA in release reports (open).
  Also touches the ship-skill Discord release notification composition.
- **WL-0MURIXAHY0031JIJ** — Send standup reports to discord using the same
  webhook as the ship skill (open). Shares the same webhook/config resolution;
  any test-isolation convention should be consistent across these items.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (target location).** The offending tests live in the shared ship
  skill test harness — currently provided by the agent-framework skill tree
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/ship`, symlinked from the SorraAgents repo), not in this
  repository's own vitest suite. This repository does not currently contain a
  `skill/ship` tree. If the operator intends the fix to land in this repository
  instead, the harness must first be vendored here (separate work).
- **Risk (scope creep).** "Fixing" this by changing production
  `discord-notify.js` could weaken real release notifications. **Mitigation:**
  prefer harness-level stubbing; add a production guard only if strictly
  necessary, and keep it opt-in.
- **Risk (false safety).** Over-mocking could hide a real Step 8.5 wiring
  regression. **Mitigation:** retain the dedicated wiring test
  (`test-run-release-discord-notify.mjs`).
- **Risk (environment coupling).** Redirecting `HOME` could affect unrelated
  behaviour of the spawned `run-release.js`/`git`/`wl` mocks. **Mitigation:**
  inject an explicit `globalConfigPath` (or stub the notifier) rather than
  changing `HOME` wholesale.
- **Failure mode.** If the harness stubs the notifier but the assertion set is
  incomplete, a future test could re-copy the real module. **Mitigation:** AC3
  regression guard.
- **Scope control.** Wiring the resolved CTA into the notification is the
  separate open item WL-0MUWEPN6X0044R43 and is **not** in scope here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: **Which repository/test suite is the target of this fix?** The seed says
  "tests for ContextHub", but this repository's vitest suite does not send any
  Discord message; the only confirmed sender is the shared ship-skill
  integration test `tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`, which copies
  the real `discord-notify.js` and executes `run-release.js` with an inherited
  `HOME`, falling back to the global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` webhook.
  Answer (operator, interactive): "Just remove that part of the test code." —
  remove the offending test code that triggers the real notification, rather
  than adding a guard/stub. Source: interactive reply.
  Note: the offending test lives in the shared ship-skill harness
  (`tests/unit/test-run-release-merge-guard.mjs`), which is not present in this
  repository; implementation must target that harness.
- Q: **Is the noisy message acceptable to leave until a later release, or must
  it be silenced now?** Answer (operator, seed intent): "This is harmless but
  noisy, remove it." — remove now. Source: interactive seed context.

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSI0DWF50070JMT** – [test-failure] tests/cli/smoke.test.ts — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MSBU4KMA004PKSR** – Code Freeze: herdr plugin blocks implement actions (banner + dialog) during ship-it process (completed)
- **WL-0MM8V55PV1Q32K7D** – Fix destructive db.import() in GitHub flows (completed)

# Problem Statement

`test_run_in_pane.sh` starts `run-in-pane.sh --exec` with `HERDR_PANE_ID` set, which runs `sleep infinity` to keep the pane alive. The test kills the wrapper bash PID but not the grandchild `sleep infinity`, which is reparented to init and inherits the script's stdout. Any invocation piped to `tail`/`head` (e.g. `bash test_run_in_pane.sh 2>&1 | tail -35`) therefore never sees EOF and hangs indefinitely.

# Users

- Developer running the test suite with piped output (e.g. `bash test_run_in_pane.sh 2>&1 | tail -35`)
- CI systems that pipe test output for log collection
- AI agent sessions that run tests in driven/child sessions (caused hangs during WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS)

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **No orphaned processes:** Running `test_run_in_pane.sh` must not leave `sleep infinity` processes after the test completes.
2. **Piped invocations complete:** `bash packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh 2>&1 | tail -35` must complete within 30 seconds.
3. **timeout survives:** `timeout 10 bash packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh` must not hang — the timeout must be able to kill the process group.
4. **Existing test behavior unchanged:** All existing test assertions must still pass.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

# Constraints

- The fix must only affect the test invocation pattern — the production `run-in-pane.sh` `--exec` behaviour (keeping panes alive for user inspection) must remain unchanged.
- Must work on Linux (GNU coreutils); `sleep infinity` is used in the production code and confirmed acceptable for the Linux target.

# Existing State

In `run-in-pane.sh` (the `--exec` block), when `HERDR_PANE_ID` is set:

```bash
sleep infinity
```

This runs as a grandchild of the test script. Killing the wrapper bash PID does not kill `sleep infinity` — it is reparented to init and stays alive, keeping stdout open.

# Desired Change

Ensure that when the test kills the wrapper process, the `sleep infinity` grandchild is also terminated. Options:

1. Kill the entire process group using `kill -- -$$` or `kill -TERM -- -${PPID}`
2. Track the `sleep infinity` PID and kill it explicitly
3. Redirect `sleep infinity` output to a file so it doesn't inherit the test's stdout/stderr

# Key Files

- `packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh` — Fix: kill the `sleep infinity` grandchild before exiting
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — Context only; the `--exec` block is correct for production use

# Related Work

- **WL-0MSAYF461006I9FP** — "run-in-pane.sh --exec busy-loops at 100% CPU keeping pane alive (read from /dev/zero)" — related fix that changed the idle mechanism to `sleep infinity`
- **WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS** — "Pi processes should start in a work item tab" — where the hang was discovered (driven child sessions hung during this work)
- **WL-0MSCA645J005YM1E** — "[test-failure] execAsync timeout kills the whole process tree (no orphaned grandchildren) — failing test" — similar process-tree cleanup issue
- **WL-0MSB447TJ000R3N8** — "Fix orphaned wl create processes left by init-pre-push-guards tests" — pattern for cleaning up orphaned test processes

## Automated related work report

Generated by find-related skill: WL-0MSB44697000K8CP, WL-0MR89VJZL001K2D9, WL-0MSI0DYZZ003MDRM — low relevance (visibility/test-suite/validator items).

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

N/A — the work item is sufficiently defined from the discovery context.

# Problem Statement

`implement.py finish` fails with a non-fast-forward error when `dev` advances concurrently (e.g. another agent pushes during the run), causing the finish phase to abort and reset the work item to `open` — losing the completed implementation.

## Users

- AI agents running `implement.py finish` as part of the multi-child workflow (epic → children implemented serially).
- Human operators managing concurrent agent sessions that each push to `dev`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When `git merge --ff-only origin/dev` fails in the fast-forward step (Step 5) of `phase_finish`, the implementation rebase/merge the child commit onto `origin/dev` (e.g. `git rebase origin/dev` on the child branch, then fast-forward dev) instead of failing.
2. When `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` fails due to non-fast-forward, the implementation retries by rebasing the feature branch onto `origin/dev` first, then retrying the push — with an explanatory comment on the work item.
3. No information is lost: the commit hash, branch name, and worktree state are preserved in a comment so a human can recover manually if automated recovery also fails.
4. The existing fast-forward logic remains unchanged for the happy path (no regression when dev has not advanced).

## Constraints

- The fix must be safe for the multi-child workflow: if multiple children are finishing serially, each child's branch must be rebased onto the then-current `origin/dev` before push.
- Must not rewrite the child's commit history in a way that breaks the pre-push hook or context-budget checks.
- The workaround already discovered (recreate worktree, rebase, push) must be automated — no manual steps required.

## Existing State

In `implement.py` `phase_finish` (around line 4206):
- `git merge --ff-only origin/dev` fails with non-fast-forward → raises `RuntimeError` → work item reset to `open`.
- `git merge --ff-only <commit_hash>` fails for the same reason → same cascade.

## Desired Change

Replace the fatal non-fast-forward failure with a retry path: rebase the child branch onto `origin/dev`, then proceed with the fast-forward merge and push.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish()` function, lines ~4200-4230
- `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` function, lines ~1439+

## Related work

- WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS — "Pi processes should start in a work item tab" (same root cause: concurrent dev pushes; workaround documented there).
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — worktree lifecycle and isolation rules.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** This fix is narrowly targeted at the non-fast-forward failure mode in `phase_finish`. Do not expand to other push-related issues.
- **Assumption:** `git rebase origin/dev` on the child branch will resolve cleanly in most cases; if conflicts arise, the fallback is a comment with manual instructions.
- **Assumption:** The child branch name can be derived from the commit hash without needing to inspect the (now-removed) worktree.
- **Risk:** Rebasing rewrites the commit hash. The pre-push hook context-budget check may need to handle the new hash.

- N/A — no interview conducted; work item description was sufficient for a complete brief.

# Analyse test code rewrite patterns to evaluate TDD value

## Problem statement

Quantitatively evaluate whether test-driven development (TDD) has delivered value in this project by measuring how often existing test code is rewritten (modified with both additions and deletions) when new features are added. Focus specifically on changes to existing tests — not new test additions — to distinguish between test evolution and test rework.

## Users

- **Project maintainer** — wants evidence-based assessment of TDD return on investment
- **AI agents** — want empirical guidance on test-writing discipline and whether pre-implementation test writing reduces downstream churn

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Primary metric delivered**: Report the proportion of test code rewritten (lines deleted + lines re-added in existing test files) when new features are committed, expressed as a percentage of all test lines changed during feature commits.

2. **Multi-angle analysis delivered**: At least 8 distinct analyses covering different dimensions (temporal trend, test area breakdown, per-file stability, domain-specific churn, test-first signal, efficiency metrics, source volatility correlation, rewrite intensity distribution).

3. **TDD value assessment delivered**: Clear interpretation of what the data suggests about TDD value — does test-first development reduce downstream rewrite rates? Is the rewrite rate acceptable or concerning?

4. **Methodology documented**: Analysis scope (mainline only, no merges), definitions (what counts as "rewrite" vs "new" vs "modification"), and limitations are clearly stated.

5. **All project test suites pass**: Running the full test suite must succeed with no regressions from any analysis tooling created.

## Constraints

- Analysis scope: mainline (dev) only, non-merge commits. Do not include feature branches, agent worktrees, or merged branches that have not been on the mainline.
- "Rewrite" defined as: an existing test file modified (status=M) with both additions and deletions — i.e., lines of existing test code removed and replaced.
- "New tests" (status=A, file added) are excluded from rewrite counts per user's explicit request.
- Existing test suite must remain passing.

## Existing state (reconnaissance findings)

Preliminary analysis of the 2216 non-merge mainline commits (2026-Q1 through 2026-Q4):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total commits (no merges) | 2216 |
| Feature commits (touching src/) | 971 (43.8%) |
| Commits touching test files | 1241 (56.0%) |
| Feature commits with test rewrites | 161 (16.6%) |
| Feature commits with new tests only | 168 (17.3%) |
| Feature commits touching any test | 369 (38.0%) |
| Lines deleted from existing tests on features | 21,303 |
| Lines added to tests on features | 24,837 |
| **Rewrite ratio (deleted / (deleted+added))** | **46.2%** |
| Average lines rewritten per affected feature commit | 102 |
| Median lines rewritten per affected feature commit | 64 |
| P95 lines rewritten | 348 |
| Test-to-source file ratio | 110.6% (532 tests / 481 src) |
| Most modified test file commits | 103 (downtime-worker.test.ts) |
| Most modified source file commits | 157 (src/tui/controller.ts) |
| Avg test deletions per source line changed | 0.17 |
| Pure test-first commits (src A + test A, no mod) | 57 (4.6%) |
| Retrofit commits (test M on existing src) | 529 |
| Test-first vs retrofit lines | 73.7% / 26.3% |

Rewrite trend by quarter (feature commits with rewrites):
- Q1: 185
- Q2: 313
- Q3: 404
- Q4: 42 (partial)

The trend shows a clear increase in rewrite activity over time.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `test/` — legacy test directory
- `tests/` — main integration and CLI test directory (272 files)
- `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` — herdr unit tests (87 files)
- `packages/shared/src/*.test.ts` — shared unit tests (9 files)
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/*.test.ts` — TUI unit tests (43 files)
- `scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` or similar — analysis tooling (new)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: Mainline-only analysis (no merges) is representative of overall project health. Branch-specific churn is excluded.
- **Assumption**: Rewrite rate alone is a meaningful TDD indicator. High rewrite rates could indicate either (a) fragile designs that TDD would address, or (b) legitimate API changes that naturally require test updates.
- **Assumption**: The project's commit history is clean — no rewrites or history surgery that would distort the data.
- **Risk**: Scope creep — the analysis could naturally expand into broader test quality metrics (coverage, mutation scores, flakiness). These should be tracked as follow-up work items, not consumed during this task.
- **Risk**: The 2026 dates in the commit history may indicate synthetic or future-dated commits, which could affect temporal analysis interpretation.

## Related work

Automated related work search found weak matches only — no work items directly addressing test churn analysis or TDD evaluation:

- **WL-0MN1X7DIT0UVXTC8** – Remove TUI browser-opening test (completed) — tangential
- **WL-0MUYI3JRC006115V** – Test: interactive item-tab root-pane cleanup (completed) — tangential
- **WL-0MKVWTYHS0FQPZ68** – Add shortcut to close selected tree item (completed) — tangential

The project has completed test-related work items covering test extraction, test API stability, and test suite improvements, but none that systematically analyse test rewrite patterns as a metric.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What proportion of test code has been rewritten when adding features?" — Answer: Primary metric is rewrite ratio = (deletions from existing test files) / (deletions + additions) on feature commits. Preliminary figure: 46.2%. Source: intake reconnaissance.
- Q: "Do not count new tests, only changes to existing tests." — Answer: New test files (status=A) excluded from rewrite count. Only modified existing test files (status=M with both additions and deletions) count. Source: user instruction.
- Q: "Provide as many different analysis as you can." — Answer: Defined 10 distinct analysis dimensions in the acceptance criteria. Source: user instruction.
- Q: "Try to split the analysis across types of test too." — Answer: Test areas classified into: herdr-unit, herdr-integration, integration, unit, cli, script, benchmark, shared-unit, tui-unit, legacy. Each area analysed separately. Source: user instruction.

# Intake Brief — Make Herdr UI refresh snappy after agent work-item updates (WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN)

## Problem statement

After an agent writes to a work item (e.g. `wl update`, `wl close`, `wl claim`), the Herdr Work Items pane can take up to 30 s to reflect the change — and when the refresh does run, the read cache has just been invalidated by the write, so the pane spawns ~4–5 cold `wl` processes (cold `wl next` measured at ~1.5 s; each warm spawn ~0.4–0.65 s) for a multi-second update. The list therefore lags behind agent activity and feels unresponsive precisely when the operator is watching an agent work.

## Users

- **Agent operators running the Herdr Work Items pane** — the primary user; they watch the list while an agent claims, updates, and closes items, and expect it to track the agent within a second or two.
  - *As an operator watching an agent work, when the agent updates or closes a work item, I want the Work Items list to reflect the change within ~2 s without me pressing `r`, so I can trust the list is current.*
  - *As an operator, when a burst of agent writes lands (claim + update + comment), I want the list to settle on the final state promptly without a refresh storm, so the pane does not thrash.*
- **Multi-pane / multi-agent setups** — several Herdr panes share one `.worklog`; each must react to writes without multiplying spawn churn or lock contention.
- **Herdr plugin and `wl` CLI maintainers** — need a detection path that is robust (fallback to polling), cheap when idle, and does not regress the existing zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Event-driven detection ≤ 2 s:** After an agent completes a work-item write against the shared `.worklog`, the Herdr Work Items pane triggers a refresh within **2 s** (wall-clock, p95 over a representative run) via an event-driven watch on the cross-process DB-change signal (state counter and/or SQLite `worklog.db`/`-wal`), without waiting for the 30 s auto-refresh tick. Verified by an automated integration test that emulates a write and asserts a refresh is triggered within the bound, plus a manual note on a real agent write.
- **Idle no-op and fallback preserved:** When nothing has changed, the pane still spawns **zero** `wl` processes per tick and the 30 s auto-refresh tick remains the fallback (no stale-forever when the watch is unavailable). Watch events are debounced/coalesced so a burst of writes causes **at most one trailing refresh** (no refresh storm). Covered by automated tests (extending the WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ and WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N guarantees).
- **End-to-end refresh ≤ 2 s:** Once triggered, a refresh of the default view attaches fresh data and renders within **2 s** wall-clock end-to-end on a representative dataset (≥ 1000 work items, ≥ 20 expanded children), measured by a repeatable benchmark and recorded in a manual verification note.
- **Input responsiveness non-regression:** Pane keyboard input stays responsive during and after the refresh (≤ 100 ms p95 input lag, consistent with WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P); the watch/refresh path must not block the TUI event loop. Covered by an automated responsiveness regression test that fails if the fix regresses.
- **Validation/testing criterion:** Automated unit + integration tests cover (a) the watch trigger and its debounce/coalescing, (b) the fallback to the 30 s tick when the watch is unavailable/fails open, and (c) the cold-refresh spawn-count reduction; a runnable performance benchmark is added to guard against regression.
- **Documentation criterion:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full suite criterion:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Do not regress the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee** (WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ): with no DB change and a fresh sync heartbeat, a tick must still spawn nothing.
- **Preserve `doRefresh` single-flight + trailing-coalescing semantics** (WL-0MSBVYBMD004007C, WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N); the watch must feed the existing gate, not bypass it.
- **Preserve visibility and typing gates:** hidden panes and open text-input overlays must still skip refresh work.
- **Fail open, never stale-forever:** any watch read error or `fs.watch` failure must fall back to the existing polling tick.
- **No new runtime dependencies** unless explicitly justified; prefer Node built-ins (`node:fs` watch).
- **No work-item data-semantics changes** and no change to `wl` write-path correctness (writes must never be served from, or leave behind, stale cache).
- **No regression for other `wl` read consumers** (Pi TUI, CLI scripts) when `wl` core is touched.
- **Cross-platform:** `fs.watch` behaviour differs by platform (Linux inotify, macOS FSEvents, Windows); the design must degrade gracefully where watching is unreliable.
- **Input responsiveness is currently acceptable** — the fix must not make the pane input-laggy.

## Existing state

- **`packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`** — `DbChangeTracker` reads the cross-process monotonic state counter (`~/.cache/wl/state/<hash>.json`) to decide whether the DB changed since the last tick; the refresh/sync scheduler gates on it. Reads only — no watch today.
- **`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`** — `doRefresh` (~L5227) with single-flight + trailing coalescing; the scheduler `refresh` task (~L6444) gated by `isDbUnchanged` + visibility + typing; the `sync` task; the resume-poll; the event subscriber (only `pane_focused` today, no work-item-update event).
- **`packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts`** — consolidated tick loop (1 s base tick) dispatching due, non-in-flight, gate-approved tasks.
- **`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`** — `runWl` spawn path (binary `wl`/`worklog`), `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`, in-process in-flight memo (WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S), `fetchNextItems` + `fetchMandatorySubsets` (2 extra `wl list`), `fetchActionableCount`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, `fetchChildrenForItem`.
- **`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`** — constructs the default `fetcher` (~L2258) and resolves the worklog dir handed to `fetcher.setWorklogDir`.
- **`src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts`** — on-disk read cache keyed by (worklog-dir, argv, version) with WAL-aware fingerprint + state counter (`bumpStateCounter` on every write; `invalidateOnWrite`); TTL default 30 s. This is why an agent write invalidates the cache and makes the next refresh cold.
- **`src/persistent-store.ts` / `src/database.ts`** — the `wl next` / `wl list` compute path (N+1 fixes landed under WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6).
- **Measurements (this machine):** `wl list` warm ≈ 0.45–0.65 s, `wl next -n 30 --include-in-progress` warm ≈ 0.4 s but cold ≈ 1.5 s; node startup ≈ 0.15 s. Default view spawns ~5 `wl` processes per refresh (next + 2 mandatory subsets + actionable count + review queue) plus one child fetch per expanded parent plus `herdr` CLI calls for agent icons. State cache dir currently holds ~175 k counter files; DB ≈ 97 MB.

## Desired change

1. **Event-driven detection.** Add a watch in the Herdr plugin on the cross-process change signal (the state-counter file and/or `worklog.db` + `-wal`) that wakes the existing scheduler/`doRefresh` path promptly (debounced) on an agent write, with the 30 s tick retained as fallback and the idle no-op preserved.
2. **Faster application.** Cut the end-to-end refresh cost on the cold path — reduce the number of `wl` spawns per refresh (e.g. consolidate the mandatory-subset/actionable-count/review-queue queries, or read the SQLite DB in-process for the pane), and/or speed up the cold `wl next`/`list` path in `wl` core (in scope). Ensure caches are warm or bypassed without a spawn storm.
3. **Wire-through.** Feed the watch into the existing gated, single-flight, coalesced `doRefresh`; keep visibility/typing gates and fail-open fallback.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` — Add a watch API (e.g. `watchDbChanges`) alongside `DbChangeTracker`: watch the state-counter file (and/or `worklog.db`/`-wal`), debounce, emit a change callback; fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Wire the watch to the gated `doRefresh`; ensure debounce + single-flight/coalescing + visibility/typing gates; reduce spawn count in the refresh path.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts` — Register/integrate the watch trigger (or expose an immediate-run hook) without disturbing the tick model.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — Reduce/parallelise `wl` spawns for the default view; extend the in-flight memo; possibly add a low-latency read path.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Construct/pass the watcher and worklog dir; teardown on pane exit.
- `src/read-cache.ts` / `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — Cache-hit/cold-path improvements (e.g. proactive warming or narrower invalidation) if needed to hit the target.
- `src/persistent-store.ts` / `src/database.ts` — Cold `wl next`/`list` performance (only if needed; keep data semantics unchanged).
- `packages/herdr/src/db-change.test.ts` (new/reused), `packages/herdr/src/worklist-inflight.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` (precedent) — tests.
- `bench/` (e.g. `bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts`) — repeatable refresh benchmark.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ** — Herdr selection list: gate background/foreground sync on DB-update check before spawning wl commands. Introduced the `DbChangeTracker` + idle no-op we must preserve and build the watch on.
- **WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3** — Central cache for wl read results to cut Herdr refresh spawn churn. The on-disk read cache whose invalidation makes post-write refreshes cold.
- **WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S** — In-process fetch memoization (F4 of the read-cache epic).
- **WL-0MSBVYBMD004007C** — Herdr worklist: in-flight guard to prevent overlapping refresh cycles.
- **WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N** — Refresh trailing/coalescing to avoid refresh storms.
- **WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P** — Hydrate task timeouts cause HERDR UI to become unresponsive to commands. Precedent: bounded timeouts, stdio isolation, p95 input-lag < 100 ms; this item's responsiveness constraint mirrors it.
- **WL-0MUY1CZES0099A04** — Herdr: UI responsiveness regression test (child of the above).
- **WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6** — Investigate and fix wl next performance bottlenecks. Prior work on the cold `wl next` path.
- **WL-0MSG8EG7P002MX2I** — Investigate WAL growth/checkpointing under concurrent writers. Relevant to watching `-wal` and to cold-read cost.
- **Pi-TUI precedents:** WL-0MKXN75CZ0QNBUJJ (*Auto-refresh TUI on DB write*), WL-0MQ3LYSPS006V60H (*TUI does not auto-refresh after CLI audit update*) — prior DB-write-triggered refresh in the sibling UI.
- **Automated find-related report** (find-related skill, keyword-based; embedded here so it survives description updates):

  **Related work items**
  - **WL-0MQOIBTHR002VMEK** – Add Guardrails to Protect Worklog Data Integrity (completed)
  - **WL-0MV16PXJ6003FEYT** – Rewrite README opening to lead with Herdr agent-orchestration role, then Worklog (completed)
  - **WL-0MLYEW3VB1GX4M8O** – Add closed count to GithubSyncResult and sync output (completed)

  **Repository file matches**
  - `standups/2026_10_10.md` — seed line for this work item
  - `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr plugin documentation
  - `CHANGELOG.md` — excluded from doc updates (managed by the release pipeline)

## Risks & assumptions

- **`fs.watch` reliability** — events can be dropped/coalesced and differ by platform/filesystem (NFS, containers). **Mitigation:** debounce, keep the 30 s tick as fallback, fail open, and test the fallback path explicitly.
- **Performance target is environment-dependent** — ≤ 2 s may be unachievable on a fully loaded host. **Mitigation:** pair the absolute target with a repeatable benchmark and a relative-improvement assertion so regression is caught regardless of host load; record a manual verification note.
- **Scope creep into `wl` core** — breadth is plugin + `wl` core, which can balloon. **Mitigation:** land the plugin-side win first; if `wl`-core work grows, split it into a child work item rather than expanding scope.
- **Watch overhead across many panes** — N watchers on one DB. **Assumption:** watching is cheap (one watcher per pane, debounced); if it proves costly, a shared watcher or heartbeat-based single-watcher can follow.
- **Correctness after write** — a watch must never serve stale data or race the write. **Mitigation:** reuse the existing state-counter/WAL fingerprint semantics; never bypass the DB-change check.
- **Assumption:** the cross-process state counter and SQLite `worklog.db`/`-wal` are the right watch targets; confirmed by reading `src/read-cache.ts`/`read-cache-cli.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts`.
- **Scope-creep risk (explicit):** any further opportunities discovered (e.g. reducing state-counter file count, WAL checkpointing) are recorded as linked work items, not absorbed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Which UI surface is in scope?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **A — Herdr plugin worklist pane only (`packages/herdr`)**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Pi TUI Worklog extension is out of scope; sibling TUI items are referenced as precedents only.
- **Q2: What is the primary symptom to fix?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **A — latency: the list takes too long to reflect an agent's change; pane input is currently responsive and must not regress**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: ACs target end-to-end latency; a responsiveness non-regression guard is included.
- **Q3: How far may the fix reach?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **B — Herdr plugin and the `wl` CLI/core**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: both the detection path (plugin) and the cold read path (`wl` core) may be changed; constraints protect other consumers.
- **Q4: What end-to-end target defines "snappy"?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **B — ≤ 2 s from agent write to list reflecting it**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: AC1/AC3 use 2 s as the measurable bound, paired with a benchmark and manual note because absolute timings are host-dependent.
- **Q5: How should the pane detect an agent's write?** — Answer (user@rgardler, interactive): **A — event-driven `fs.watch` on the cross-process state counter / SQLite WAL, keeping the 30 s tick as fallback**. Source: interactive reply. Implication: no `wl` write-path contract change is required; the existing `DbChangeTracker`/state-counter signal is reused as the watch target, with fail-open fallback.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-12T15:22:47: plan skill decomposed this item into 6 children in test-first dependency order (verification harness → watch primitive → wiring → cold-refresh cost; plus responsiveness guard and docs/suite). Dependency edges wired; acceptance-criteria coverage verified at 100% against the 7 parent ACs (normalised the numbered AC list to bullets so automated coverage tooling can parse it — wording unchanged).

## Appendix: planning Q&A

The planning session asked no new questions: the intake Appendix (Q1–Q5, user@rgardler) already answered the scope (Herdr plugin + `wl` core), the primary symptom (latency; input responsiveness must not regress), the end-to-end target (≤ 2 s from agent write), and the detection approach (event-driven `fs.watch` on the state counter / SQLite WAL, 30 s tick as fallback). Decisions and assumptions taken during planning:

- **Delivery approach** — land the plugin-side event-driven watch and spawn consolidation first; any `wl`-core cold-path work that grows beyond the plugin-side win is split into a separate child (per the intake scope-creep mitigation).
- **In-process read option** — an in-process SQLite read path is feasible (`better-sqlite3` is already a root dependency and `@worklog/shared` re-exports the database); it is an implementation option for the cold-refresh child, not a requirement.
- **Priority mapping** — core watch/wiring/cold-cost children are `high`; test/benchmark/docs children are `medium`.
- **Coverage note** — the shared tree-coverage helper parses only bulleted ACs; parent ACs were converted from numbered to bulleted form (no wording change) so the coverage review is substantive rather than vacuous.

Discovered from WL-0MURJ0LFH002O95I.

The r i (producer interview) fix added tab focus to run-in-pane.sh: a focused pane anchored to a work-item-ID tab now runs herdr tab focus before the pane zoom, because pane zoom alone cannot switch tabs.

shared/send-to-pi.sh has the same latent gap: its --focus path only runs pane zoom. No bundled agent shortcut currently combines focus: true with a work-item ID (P n has no <id>, so it opens in the current tab — a no-op today), so this is not user-visible yet. If a future --focus agent shortcut carries an <id>, its pane would open in the work-item-ID tab without focusing it.

Apply the same best-effort tab-focus (herdr pane get <pane> -> herdr tab focus) to send-to-pi.sh, mirroring run-in-pane.sh, with bash tests in packages/herdr/shared/tests/.
data.title: Focus parity: send-to-pi.sh should focus the item tab for focused agent shortcuts

# Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item tab existence

## Problem statement

The "in progress" marker shown in the Herdr selection list is unreliable: it is
derived from the worklog `in-progress` status, which is maintained by the
hydrator — a self-healing loop that decides whether a claimed item is genuinely
being worked on by matching the item ID against live **pane titles**
(`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`). That pane-title matching predates the
one-tab-per-work-item convention: every interactive/downtime dispatch now places
its agent pane in a tab labelled with the **exact work-item ID**
(`getItemTabAnchor` / `findTabByLabel` in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`).
Panes can be re-parented, renamed, truncated or multi-pane per tab, so pane-title
matching produces false negatives (→ wrong demotion, marker disappears while work
continues) and is needlessly complex.

## Users

- Herdr operator selecting the next work item from the selection list.
- Downtime dispatcher / plugin panes that rely on the hydrator to release stale
  `in-progress` claims so the item re-enters the dispatchable pool.

Example user stories:

- As a Herdr operator, I want the selection list's in-progress marker to reflect
  reality — an item is "being worked on" iff a tab named after its work-item ID
  exists in my workspace — so I can trust the list without opening tabs.
- As a dispatched agent, I want my claimed item left `in-progress` for as long as
  my work-item tab is open, so my claim is never released underneath me.
- As an operator, I want a stale claim (no work-item tab) released automatically
  and periodically so abandoned items return to the dispatchable pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a tab in the current workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`) has a label **equal to** the work-item ID; a tab label that merely *contains* the ID does not count, and a pane title containing the ID no longer counts on its own. Verified by unit tests over a pure tab-matching helper.
- [ ] The hydrator's active detection is switched from `herdr pane list` + pane-title ID extraction to `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` + exact tab label match; the pane-matching seam/types (`HydratorPane`, `listActivePanes`, `collectPaneWorkItemIds`, `isActivePaneMatch`) are replaced by tab equivalents. Verified by code review + updated `hydrator.test.ts` (no `pane list` spawn asserted).
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` → `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An item with a matching tab is never demoted. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] The signal is refreshed periodically from the selection list: the existing 30 s hydrate task (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) and the hidden→visible focus-resume hook both re-evaluate tab existence, so a closed work-item tab clears the marker within one cadence and an opened tab keeps it. Verified by existing scheduler/visibility tests plus a tab-based hydration test.
- [ ] Fail-open preserved: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr tab list` aborts the cycle without demoting, and tabs outside the current workspace never mark an item active. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (notably the hydrator module header, `pane-title.ts` rationale comment and `herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` if it references pane-title matching).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the worklog status/stage vocabulary or the demotion outcome rules.
- Keep the bounded/responsive hydrator contract (per-step timeout, per-tick cap,
  stdio isolation, fail-open) unchanged; only the "which items are active" lookup
  changes.
- Reuse the existing tab listing/parsing (`listTabsInWorkspace`,
  `parseTabListOutput`, `findTabByLabel`) rather than adding a second parser.
- Retain exports still used elsewhere: `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
  (`ship-guard.ts`) and `isActiveBlocker` (`stalled-work.ts`).
- No CLI or socket API change; `herdr tab list` is already used by the plugin.
- Write in UK English; follow the project's test/build conventions.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — fetches `wl list --status in-progress`,
  fetches `herdr pane list [--workspace <id>]`, collects work-item IDs from pane
  labels (`WORK_ITEM_ID_REGEX` over `pane.label`), and demotes items with no
  matching pane. Exposes pure helpers (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`,
  `isActivePaneMatch`, `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — creates the hydrator runner with
  `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, runs it every 30 s (`hydrate`
  task) and on hidden→visible focus-resume. The selection list's in-progress
  marker (`statusIcon(item.status)`) and Group N ordering (`status ===
  'in-progress'`) are driven by the worklog status this loop maintains.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — already lists/creates tabs labelled
  with the exact item ID: `listTabsInWorkspace`, `parseTabListOutput`,
  `findTabByLabel`, `getItemTabAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — truncation helper exists specifically so
  the ID survives in pane titles for the hydrator; this rationale becomes obsolete
  for matching (the helper may remain for human-readable titles).

## Desired change

Replace the hydrator's pane-title-based "is this item active" signal with a
tab-label-based one:

1. Add a pure helper that, given the tabs of the current workspace, returns the
   set of work-item IDs whose tab label matches exactly (e.g.
   `collectTabWorkItemIds(tabs)` / `hasItemTab(itemId, tabs)`).
2. Change `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes` → `listTabs(workspaceId)` backed by
   `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` (reusing the shared parser), and update
   `runHydrationOnce` to use tab membership.
3. Keep `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`,
   `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` and the bounded-run machinery intact.
4. Update tests and the module/doc comments to describe tab-based detection.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — replace pane matching with exact tab-label matching; rename seam/types/helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — reuse/export `listTabsInWorkspace` / `parseTabListOutput` / `findTabByLabel` for the hydrator's tab lookup.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring (workspace id, cadence, focus-resume); update comments if needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — rewrite active-pane cases as active-tab cases; add exact-match, workspace-scope and fail-open cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts` — replace `makeWorstCasePanes` with tab fixtures and update the exec router to answer `tab list`.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — update to the tab-based deps.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — adjust/retire the "hydrator matches pane titles" rationale comment.
- `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` — update if it documents pane-title matching for the hydrator.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI — Herdr hydrator: rescue `in_progress` work items with no active pane (parent of the pane-matching design).
- WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US — Hydrator: demote stale `in_progress` items (child, currently blocked).
- WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ / WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO / WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX — bounded/isolated hydrate steps (contract to preserve).
- WL-0MUKXFWLD006A8XI / WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — item-ID tab anchor and interactive dispatch wiring (the tab-per-item convention this builds on).
- WL-0MUY1CS9E006ZLS0 — re-based Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on `status` (the marker this work makes reliable).
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — per-row agent-status icon (separate, richer herdr agent-reporting signal; out of scope here).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLX5OADB1TECIZV** – Testing: automation - create work item (completed)
- **WL-0MM0DTK1B1Z0VMIB** – wl list --stage in_review returns nothing while --json shows content (completed)
- **WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN** – Herdr: re-enable terminal drag-select while keeping mouse support (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, existence, herdr (+17 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, existence, herdr (+17 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, herdr, iff (+15 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "the logic for discovering when an item is being worked
  on" is the hydrator's active detection; the selection-list in-progress marker
  follows from the status the hydrator maintains. The agent-status icon
  (`AgentTracker`, herdr `agent list`) is a distinct feature and is not changed.
- **Assumption:** tabs are labelled with the exact work-item ID
  (`getItemTabAnchor` / `findTabByLabel` convention), so exact label equality is
  the correct match; substring matching is rejected to avoid false positives.
- **Assumption:** `herdr tab list` returns `result.tabs[].label` (and `tab_id`),
  as parsed by `parseTabListOutput`; no new herdr capability is required.
- **Risk:** legacy tabs created before the item-ID convention (or hand-created
  tabs) may not be labelled with the ID, so an item could be demoted while a
  legacy pane is still active. Mitigation: the item-ID tab convention is now the
  only dispatch path; document the change.
- **Risk:** a tab may outlive its agent (kept open after the agent finishes),
  leaving an item `in-progress`. This matches the requested rule (tab = worked
  on); operators close the tab to release the item.
- **Scope-creep risk:** sharing the signal with `AgentTracker` or the agent-status
  icon. Record any such opportunity as a linked follow-up work item, not in scope
  here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which 'logic for discovering when an item is being worked on' should switch
  to tab existence: the hydrator's stale-claim detection, or a new
  display-layer marker?" — **Assumed answer** (Map, from the intake seed): the
  hydrator's stale-claim detection, whose status output drives the selection-list
  in-progress marker. Evidence: `hydrator.ts` is the only discovery logic
  (pane-title matching predating per-item tabs); the worklist runs it every 30 s
  and on focus-resume. Source: interactive intake request; recorded as an
  assumption for producer confirmation at review.
- Q: "Does tab 'matching the work item ID' mean exact label equality or
  contains?" — **Assumed answer** (Map): exact equality, consistent with
  `findTabByLabel` ("never a substring/prefix match") and `getItemTabAnchor`
  (tab labelled exactly the item ID). Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Should a matching tab require a live pane inside it?" — **Assumed answer**
  (Map): no — tab existence is the signal, per the seed request ("If there is a
  tab ... then it is being worked on"). Source: interactive intake request.

## Plan (decomposition)

Planned 2026-10-10. Three child work items, created in dependency order:

1. **WL-0MV24RM9I0051GEF** — Hydrator: switch active detection to exact tab-label
   matching (core + test migration). Vertical slice: `hydrator.ts` types, pure
   helpers, orchestration and production wiring, plus the structural test/fixture
   migration needed to keep the package green.
2. **WL-0MV24T2VJ007Q49J** — Verification: tab-matching edge cases (exact match,
   substring rejection, workspace scoping, fail-open, no pane-list spawn) plus
   the responsiveness-suite migration. Depends on the core item.
3. **WL-0MV25EE4E0028KDI** — Docs: hydrator module header, `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`,
   `packages/herdr/README.md` and the `pane-title.ts` rationale comment. Depends on
   the core item.

Test-first: the core item follows TDD (tab-matching tests written/extended before
the implementation); the verification item adds the exhaustive behavioural
coverage demanded by this item's ACs.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-10 — Created the three child items above and wired the dependency
  edges (verification → core; docs → core).
- 2026-10-10 — Reformatted the multi-line acceptance-criteria bullets into
  single-line bullets so automated AC-coverage extraction works (no intent
  change; the prior line wrapping truncated every AC to its first line).

# Deduplicate legacy test/ vs tests/ files and delete verbatim subsets

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want duplicate and verbatim-subset test files removed, so the suite does not carry redundant coverage that inflates runtime and maintenance cost without improving defect detection.

## Background

The test-churn analysis (WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ) found 14 pairs of same-named test files across parallel directories, several of which are duplicate coverage rather than legitimate layering. Confirmed examples:

- `tests/validator.test.ts` (12 lines) is a verbatim subset of `test/validator.test.ts` (133 lines) — both run the same CLI-doc validator assertion.
- `test/migrations.test.ts` (66 lines) and `tests/migrations.test.ts` (138 lines) — legacy vs modern.
- `test/validator.test.ts` and `tests/validator.test.ts`.
- `tests/unit/icons.test.ts`, `tests/herdr/icons.test.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/icons.test.ts` — three icons test files.

This matches the existing anti-pattern "Duplicates of Existing Core Coverage" in `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (canonical guidance lives in SorraAgents).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The legacy `test/` directory is triaged: each file is classified as duplicate, subset, superseded, or genuinely unique.
- Verbatim subsets and exact duplicates are deleted (not rewritten under a new name).
- Genuinely unique coverage from legacy files is migrated into the corresponding modern test file before deletion.
- Remaining same-named files across directories are justified in a short comment or documentation note (legitimate layer difference only).
- The full test suite passes with no reduction in meaningful coverage; any removed assertions are accounted for.
- Suite runtime and test count are measured before and after and reported on the work item.
- The change is recorded in the CHANGELOG.

## Related work

- WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ (analysis evidence)
- SorraAgents `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (anti-pattern 4)

# Intake Brief: Split downtime-worker.test.ts and cap mocks per test

**Work Item:** WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX
**Issue Type:** task
**Priority:** medium

## Problem statement

The single largest test file in the repository (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, 13,103 lines) dominates 10% of the entire test suite with 100 describe blocks, 664 `vi.fn()` calls, and 107 mainline commits. This monolithic file is hard to navigate, fragile under refactoring, and masks individual test failures under noise.

## Users

- **Maintainer / AI agent** — wants focused test files that are reviewable, faster to navigate, and less fragile.
- **Reviewer** — wants small, coherent test files where each file covers one concern with a bounded number of mocks.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **File split by concern.** `downtime-worker.test.ts` is split into multiple focused test files targeting ≤ 2,000 lines each. Logical groupings follow existing describe-block boundaries (e.g. dispatch wiring, tier selection, scheduling, audit trail, idle detection, worker orchestrator).

2. **Shared fixtures/helpers.** A shared fixture module replaces duplicated per-test setup. No test re-implements another group's setup.

3. **Mock budget enforced.** A per-test mock cap is agreed and enforced — either via a lint/CI check (failing tests exceeding N `vi.fn()`/mock declarations) or equivalent mechanism — and the limit is documented. The cap value N is determined from analysis of existing test mock density.

4. **Observable-outcome assertions.** Assertions prefer observable outcomes over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators, per SorraAgents `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

5. **All tests pass, no coverage lost.** All moved tests still pass in the new file locations. Any assertions deliberately dropped are justified and documented on the work item.

6. **Runtime measured.** Suite runtime for this module is measured before and after splitting, and the results are reported as a comment on the work item.

## Constraints

- Do not change production code.
- Do not lose test coverage — every existing test must be preserved unless deliberately dropped (with justification).
- All project test suites must pass after the split.
- File names should follow existing conventions (e.g. `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`).
- The shared fixture module must be importable by all split test files.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`: 13,103 lines, 100 `describe` blocks, 664 `vi.fn()` calls.
- Shared `makeDeps()` function creates mock dependencies (~20 mocks per call).
- Related analysis in WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ confirms this as the most-churned test file (103 commits).
- Related work: WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL (downtime worker test suite, completed).

## Desired change

Split the monolithic file into concern-specific files, introduce a shared fixture module, enforce a mock budget per test, and migrate assertions toward observable outcomes where feasible.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Source file to split
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — Or new shared fixture module
- `packages/herdr/src/downt-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — New file (dispatch wiring, tier selection)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` — New file (worker orchestration)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.idle.test.ts` — New file (idle detection, idle tracker)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit.test.ts` — New file (audit trail, audit tier)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` — New file (settings clamps, enable/disable)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.pane.test.ts` — New file (pane spawn, pane lifecycle)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The existing describe-block boundaries provide logical groupings for file splits. If they do not, the split strategy should be re-evaluated during implementation.
- **Assumption:** A per-test mock budget of 5–8 `vi.fn()` is a reasonable starting point. This should be validated against existing test density.
- **Risk: Scope creep.** The mock-budget enforcement mechanism (lint/CI check) could expand into a broader linting framework. Track this as a follow-up work item, not consumed here.
- **Risk: Import coupling.** Shared fixtures must not introduce circular imports between test files. Validate import graph after the split.
- **Risk: Assertion migration scope.** Moving `toHaveBeenCalledWith` assertions to observable-outcome assertions could change test semantics. Any such changes must be carefully reviewed and justified.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ** — Test code rewrite pattern analysis (evidence: this is the most churned test file)
- **WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL** — Downtime worker test suite (test-first, completed)
- **SorraAgents test-writing-guidelines.md** — Prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith`

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What mock budget number N per test?" — Answer: To be determined during implementation based on analysis of existing test mock density. Suggested starting point: 5–8 `vi.fn()` per test, with the fixture module's shared mocks excluded from the count.
- Q: "What exact file split boundaries?" — Answer: To be determined during implementation. Proposed split follows existing describe-block groupings (dispatch, orchestrator, idle, audit, settings, pane).
- Q: "Should the mock budget be enforced via lint or CI?" — Answer: A lint/CI check is the preferred mechanism (e.g. a custom ESLint rule or Vitest plugin). If impractical, a documented convention with manual enforcement is acceptable for the first pass.

# Intake: Create shared fixture module

**Work Item:** Child of WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX
**Issue Type:** task
**Priority:** high

## Problem statement

The monolithic `downtime-worker.test.ts` (13,103 lines) contains a `makeDeps()` function (~20 vi.fn() mocks per call) and various shared test setup patterns that are duplicated or scattered across the file. These need to be extracted into a proper shared fixture module that all split test files can import.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Extract `makeDeps()`.** The `makeDeps(overrides)` function is moved from `downtime-worker.test.ts` into `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` (or a dedicated helpers module). It provides default mocked `DowntimeWorkerDeps` and merges overrides.

2. **Extract common test setup.** Any other per-test setup patterns (e.g. temporary directory creation, file-system setup, mock configuration) that are reused across multiple describe blocks are extracted into the fixture module.

3. **All split test files import from the fixture module.** No split test file re-implements `makeDeps()` or duplicate setup logic.

4. **No functional change.** The extracted fixtures behave identically to the originals — all existing tests pass with the fixture module in place.

5. **Type-safe exports.** The fixture module exports typed functions and constants with JSDoc comments explaining each export's purpose.

# Intake: Enforce per-test mock budget

**Work Item:** Child of WL-0MV28X3SL005R5KX
**Issue Type:** task
**Priority:** medium
**Dependencies:** WL-0MV4V0V8Z003PBQ2 (shared fixture module)

## Problem statement

The monolithic `downtime-worker.test.ts` has 664 `vi.fn()` calls spread across 100 describe blocks. After splitting, each test file should have a bounded number of mocks per test to improve test clarity and maintainability.

## Analysis

From analysis of the existing file:
- Total `vi.fn()` calls: ~664 across ~128 describe blocks
- Average: ~5.2 `vi.fn()` per describe block
- The `makeDeps()` fixture creates ~20 default mocks per call (excluded from per-test count — these are shared infrastructure)
- Tests that override individual mocks via `makeDeps({ getNextItem: vi.fn() })` add 1–5 additional mocks on top

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mock cap determined.** Based on the analysis above, agree on a per-test mock cap N. Suggested: **5 `vi.fn()` overrides per test** (excluding the ~20 default mocks from `makeDeps()`). This is a reasonable cap for focused tests.

2. **Enforcement mechanism implemented.** Choose one of:
   - **Option A (preferred):** A lightweight ESLint rule that flags test files with more than N `vi.fn()` calls per `it()` block.
   - **Option B:** A CI check script that counts `vi.fn()` calls per test and fails if the cap is exceeded.
   - **Option C:** Documented convention in `TESTING.md` with manual enforcement (acceptable for first pass).

3. **All split test files comply.** Every new test file respects the mock budget. Tests exceeding the cap are refactored (e.g., by extracting more setup into the fixture module).

4. **Mock budget documented.** The cap N, its rationale, and enforcement mechanism are documented in the fixture module or a dedicated testing guide.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — Where mock budget is enforced and documented
- `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` — Split test files

## Summary

Vitest additions covering drag-to-scroll in the Herdr worklist list and detail views, written before implementation (test-first). Covers parent ACs 1–6: threshold dead-zone, list drag rows + selection invariance, detail drag lines + clamping, drag-release inert, hover on button-less motion, drag inert in filter mode, and the updated motion-branch tests for the hover-vs-drag split.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Suite exercises a pure `mapMouseDrag(state, ev, dragState, termSize)` returning `drag-start` / `drag-list` / `drag-detail` / null, including the threshold dead-zone where movement at or below `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS` is inert (parent AC5)
- Suite covers list drag: left-button-held vertical motion past the threshold yields `drag-list` with whole-row deltas proportional to movement, and `WorkItemListState.scrollBy` changes `scrollOffset` while `selectedIndex` is unchanged (parent AC1)
- Suite covers detail drag: the same gesture in detail mode yields `drag-detail` with 1 terminal row ≈ 1 line, clamped to the content bounds via the existing detail scroll clamp (parent AC2)
- Suite covers drag-vs-click isolation: a press that crosses the threshold yields no `select-row`/`open-detail`, its release is inert, and a press–release that never crosses the threshold still selects (or double-clicks) as before (parent AC3)
- Suite covers hover/drag separation: button-less motion (`(button & 3) === 3`) maps to `hover-row`/`hover-none` while left-button-held motion maps to drag (parent AC4)
- Suite covers threshold/clamping edges: sub-threshold drags are inert; drags past the content bounds clamp at 0/max without overscroll or selection movement (parent AC5)
- Suite covers filter-mode inertness: drag motion in filter mode yields null (out of scope)
- New tests live in `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts`; the existing motion-branch guard tests are updated to reflect the hover-vs-drag split, and the suite runs green via the herdr vitest run

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` with drag describe blocks, following the existing pure-function test pattern (`press`, `TERM_80x24`, `makeListState` fixtures)
- Add a `dragState` test helper mirroring `MouseClickState`; assert on the mapper's return value and on state effects after `handleMouseInput`
- Update the existing "drag-motion guard and button codes" describe block so motion coverage reflects hover (button-less) vs drag (left-held)

## Dependencies

None — created first (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` additions (new + updated drag tests)
- Red-phase evidence recorded as a comment on the parent

Thread the drag tracker through `handleMouseInput`, dispatch drag actions (restoring the pre-press selection on activation), and split the motion branch of `mapMouseToAction` into hover (button-less) vs drag (left-held). Integration slice for WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK.

## Goal
Fix the implement skill's non-fast-forward push recovery, which crashes with NameError and strands committed work.

## Evidence
Running `implement.py finish WL-0MV4UZ6C4007XDGI` while `dev` advanced concurrently (another drive pushing) produced:

```
File ".../skill/implement/scripts/implement.py", line 4307, in phase_finish
    cwd=cwd,
NameError: name 'cwd' is not defined
```

The `PushNonFastForwardError` handler (around line 4297-4347) calls `run_cmd(["git","rebase","origin/dev"], cwd=cwd)`, but `cwd` is not defined in `phase_finish`. It should be `cwd=worktree_path` (the worktree variable used elsewhere in the function). Because the worktree is removed earlier (step 6) and the crash occurs at push (step 7), committed work is left on a local branch while the item is reset to `open`, and re-running `start` then fails because the branch already exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The `PushNonFastForwardError` handler rebases in the correct directory and does not raise NameError.
- A regression test covers a non-fast-forward push where `dev` advanced concurrently.
- Re-running `finish` after a non-fast-forward recovers the committed work instead of stranding it.

The skill is symlinked from `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (consumer: ContextHub).
