data.description:
# Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap

**Issue type:** feature · **Priority:** medium · **Stage:** intake (draft)

## Problem statement

When the llm-proxy rejects requests with "all providers exhausted",
"all providers unavailable", or "no provider is available during the current
scheduled time window" (HTTP 503), the in-pane recovery loop classifies the
error as a retryable `SERVER_ERROR` and waits out the server-requested
`Retry-After`. While a pane sits in that backoff it holds **no** proxy slot,
so the proxy reports idle and the herdr mode-switch worker flips the shared
proxy to **cheap** on the operator idle window. Cheap mode has *more* slots
than fast (3 vs 1 — `WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM`), so it adds concurrency, and cheap
windows are observed to correlate with exhaustion bursts. Nothing durably
records that a work item is waiting *because the model was unavailable*, so
neither the cheap-switch decision nor the dispatcher can see the difference
between "quiet" and "blocked on a throttled provider".

## Users

- **Operator/producer** running unattended (downtime) dispatch overnight, who
  wants queued work to resume as soon as a model returns, without piling new
  concurrent requests onto an already-exhausted provider pool.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher**, which must know when a waiting job is
  eligible to resume and must not spawn more work while the pool is throttled.

Example user stories:

- As an operator, when cloud providers are exhausted, I want the proxy to stay
  in fast mode (or at least not add concurrency) so that my queued jobs do not
  exhaust the pool further.
- As the downtime dispatcher, when a model cooldown elapses, I want to resume
  exactly one waiting pane with a `continue` message rather than opening a
  brand-new pane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Durable cooldown record.** When a pane's recovery loop
      classifies a model-unavailable error (`SERVER_ERROR` exhaustion
      patterns) and starts a backoff, a durable, machine-readable record is
      written carrying item id, kind, reason, and `cooldownUntil`; it is
      cleared on the next successful provider response. Verified by unit tests
      of the writer/reader and a write→read→clear round-trip test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Cheap-switch gate.** While at least one active model-cooldown
      exists (`cooldownUntil` in the future), the downtime leader's
      `mode-switch-worker.tick()` does **not** POST `cheap`; the hold is
      bounded by `cooldownUntil` (no latch) and the fast-on-command path is
      unaffected. Verified by mode-switch-worker unit tests (cooldown present
      / expired / absent / unreadable).
- [ ] **AC3 — Bounded wake.** At/after `cooldownUntil`, the dispatcher resumes
      **at most one** model-cooldown job via the existing stalled-resume path
      (literal `continue` to a live pane, or relaunch pi `--continue` in an
      exited pane), reusing the attempt-cap and `needsProducerReview`
      exclusions. Verified by dispatcher/stalled-work tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Cross-root gate.** A cooldown recorded in any worklog root
      suppresses the machine-wide (shared-proxy) cheap switch. Verified by an
      integration test spanning two roots.
- [ ] **AC5 — Fail-closed and bounded default.** An unreadable/absent signal
      never causes a premature cheap switch (existing fail-closed contract
      preserved); an absent/unparseable `Retry-After` yields a **bounded**
      default cooldown rather than an unbounded hold. Verified by tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests.** Unit + integration tests cover detection, gating, wake,
      cross-root, and failure paths; a regression test proves the previous
      client-side drain is **not** reintroduced (no slot-count completion
      gate, no dispatch pause, no unbounded latch).
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
      the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`,
      `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`, and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
      changes.

## Constraints

- **Must not reintroduce the withdrawn client drain** (`WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR`):
  no client-side slot-count completion gate, no dispatch pause, no unbounded
  latch. The proxy's own server-side bounded drain is unchanged and stays
  authoritative.
- The cheap-switch gate is **bounded by `cooldownUntil`**; it must never block
  the fast-on-command path (`onOperatorCommand`).
- Live pool sizing is fast = 1 slot, cheap = 3 slots
  (`WL-0MUWF763Q003MGUM`), i.e. cheap *increases* concurrency; the gate's only
  purpose is to avoid adding concurrency during known provider exhaustion.
- The mode-switch worker is leader-only and machine-wide, so the cooldown
  signal must be machine-wide for cross-root correctness.
- First increment must not require a new proxy endpoint; a proxy
  provider-availability endpoint is a **follow-up**, not in scope.
- The recovery loop lives in the TUI extension and the consumer in the herdr
  package, so the on-disk signal format is a cross-package contract and must
  be versioned/tolerant (unknown fields ignored).

## Existing state

- **Detection exists, but is ephemeral.** `error-patterns.ts` classifies the
  exhaustion bodies as `SERVER_ERROR`; `resolveRetryDelay()` /
  `parseRetryAfterHeaders()` (`retry-logic.ts`) extract the server-requested
  delay (ceiling 6 h) and `register-recovery.ts:406` computes it. The result
  lives only in in-memory `RetryState`.
- **No durable model-cooldown state.** The rolling
  `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (`downtime-log.ts`) has dispatch markers
  and pane-close `reasonCode`s but no cooldown entry; the worklog
  `needsProducerReview` flag is unrelated.
- **Wake machinery already exists.** `classifyStalledPane` /
  `resumeStalledPane` (`stalled-work.ts`) prompt a live pane with the literal
  `continue`, or relaunch pi `--continue` in an exited pane, and the
  dispatcher already prefers resuming a stalled pane over opening a new one
  (`WL-0MUMA5OMH0024PN1`). Its trigger is "not working ≥ threshold", gated by
  the non-terminal cooldown and attempt cap — with **no model-availability
  input**.
- **The cheap path is blind.** `mode-switch-worker.tick()` switches to cheap on
  `operator idle ≥ threshold AND evaluateIdle(proxyStatus)`; a pane in backoff
  holds zero slots, so this looks idle.
- **The proxy cannot report exhaustion today.** `LlamaStatus`
  (`/llama/local/status`) exposes local server/slot/lease state only; there is
  no provider-availability field.

## Desired change

1. **Emit/clear a durable cooldown marker.** On `SERVER_ERROR` exhaustion in
   `register-recovery.ts`, write a record with `cooldownUntil = now + delayMs`
   (item id, kind, reason), machine-wide so any root can read it; clear it when
   `createRetryHintCapturingFetch` observes the next 2xx.
2. **Gate the cheap switch.** Read the marker in the leader's `tick()` (same
   pattern as `readSharedActivity`); while any cooldown is active, hold fast.
3. **Wake one job at expiry.** Feed expired cooldown candidates into the
   existing stalled-resume path so exactly one pane is resumed.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts` — the versioned cooldown contract and
  tolerant reader/writer shared by both packages (new).
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.test.ts` — contract tests (new).
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts` — coordination-dir resolver
  (delegates to the shared resolver; single source of truth).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` — writes
  the cooldown marker on `SERVER_ERROR`, clears it on the next 2xx.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts` — exposes the
  resolved cooldown (`cooldownUntil`).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts` — bounded
  default cooldown in the recovery configuration.
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` — reads the cooldown signal and
  gates the cheap switch.
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` — gate unit tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/stalled-work.ts` — expired-cooldown candidate source.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — dispatcher branch that resumes one
  cooldown candidate at expiry.
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`,
  `packages/herdr/README.md` — behaviour and contract documentation.

**Corrections from the predicted list (plan time):**
`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` is **dropped** — the signal is
machine-wide, not the per-root dispatch log (decision Q2 = A). The bounded
default lives in the recovery configuration in the TUI extension (which owns
the cooldown computation), not in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`; herdr only
reads the resulting signal.

## Risks and assumptions

- **R: Waking before providers return just re-fails** and burns the per-item
  attempt budget until `needsProducerReview` trips. **Mitigation:** gate the
  wake strictly on `cooldownUntil`; prefer a proxy provider-availability
  signal when one exists (follow-up).
- **R: The premise is unproven.** Cheap mode may help (local-first) or hurt
  (more concurrency) depending on why providers are exhausted.
  **Mitigation:** RESOLVED BY DECISION — the producer accepted the premise
  (interview round 2, Q1 = B): the cooldown machinery is built without a Phase 0
  log-mining gate, so this risk remains open and accepted, not mitigated.
- **R: `Retry-After` may be absent**, making the cooldown best-effort.
  **Mitigation:** bounded default cooldown setting; document best-effort.
- **R: Cross-root staleness** — a crashed pane leaves a stale marker.
  **Mitigation:** `cooldownUntil` TTL + clear-on-success + fail-closed reads.
- **R: Scope creep** into proxy (cross-repo) changes. **Mitigation:** record
  proxy endpoint work as a linked follow-up, not in this item.
- **A1 (VERIFIED at plan time):** the recovery loop can extract the item
  id/kind from `ctx` session entries best-effort. Verified: the TUI extension
  has no herdr import and no pane-label access, so the marker is keyed by
  `paneId`/`sessionId` (plus a best-effort `itemId`) and the dispatcher resolves
  item and kind from the pane label it already reads for the stalled scan. See
  "Plan-time verification".
- **A2 (CONFIRMED by decision Q2 = A):** a machine-wide JSON file in the
  coordination directory (`~/.herdr/downtime/`, alongside `mode-activity.json`)
  is the transport for the first increment, implemented as a versioned shared
  contract (`@worklog/shared/model-cooldown`).

## Decisions (interview round 2 — resolved)

Producer answers recorded 2026-10-12 in the plan session (session id in the
work-item comments):

1. **Build now vs investigate first → BUILD NOW (option B).** The cooldown
   machinery is built without a Phase 0 log-mining gate; the operator accepts
   that "cheap windows worsen exhaustion" is not yet proven. Consequence: no
   investigation gate in the plan; the premise risk stays open and is recorded
   in the appendix. There is therefore **no Phase 0 gate child**.
2. **Cooldown signal source → CLIENT RECOVERY-LOOP MARKER (option A).** The TUI
   recovery loop writes and clears a versioned, machine-wide JSON marker in the
   machine coordination directory (`HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` or
   `~/.herdr/downtime/`, alongside `mode-activity.json`), best-effort from
   `Retry-After`. A proxy provider-availability endpoint is a separate
   follow-up, not in scope.
3. **Wake trigger → STRICTLY AT/AFTER `cooldownUntil`, ONE JOB PER CYCLE
   (option A).** The wake reuses the existing stalled-resume path and its
   safety gates (attempt cap, `needsProducerReview`); no early wake and no
   batch wake.

**Plan-time verification of assumption A1:** the TUI recovery loop has no
herdr import and no pane-label access, so it cannot derive `itemId`/`kind`
from the pane label. The marker therefore carries `cooldownUntil`, `reason`,
`paneId` (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and `sessionId`, with `itemId` derived best-effort
from session entries (`ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`); the herdr dispatcher
resolves `itemId` + `kind` from the pane label it already reads for the stalled
scan (`paneLabelItemId`, `downtime-worker.ts`). The record format is versioned
JSON with unknown fields ignored.


## Plan (features)

Decomposed 2026-10-12 into 7 vertical-slice child items, created test-first
(the contract slice first, then the behaviour slices, then documentation and
verification). No Phase 0 investigation gate (decision Q1 = B).

| # | Child | Type | Depends on | Parent ACs |
|---|-------|------|------------|------------|
| 1 | `WL-0MV563825002R9Y1` Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader | task | — | AC1, AC6 |
| 2 | `WL-0MV5638J1006URXA` Recovery loop records durable cooldown | feature | 1 | AC1 |
| 3 | `WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ` Cheap-switch gate honours model cooldowns | feature | 1 | AC2, AC4 |
| 4 | `WL-0MV5639GG00085Q7` Bounded wake of one cooled-down job | feature | 1 | AC3 |
| 5 | `WL-0MV5639X70029BOI` Bounded default cooldown and fail-closed hardening | feature | 2 | AC5 |
| 6 | `WL-0MV563ADO008FT6H` Cooldown behaviour documentation | docs | 2,3,4,5 | AC7 |
| 7 | `WL-0MV563AU2007FM56` Cooldown regression guard and full-suite verification | task | 2,3,4,5 | AC6, AC8 |

Test-first ordering: child 1 (the contract/verification slice) is created first
and blocks every behaviour child; children 2–5 each write their tests before
their implementation; children 6–7 verify and document the finished behaviour.

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-12T11:13Z — interview round 2 asked (3 multiple-choice questions, each
  with an explicit agent recommendation); questions recorded verbatim as a
  work-item comment.
- 2026-10-12T11:14Z — producer answered B / A / A; questions resolved in the
  appendix above.
- 2026-10-12T11:29Z — feature breakdown produced and reviewed; 7 children
  created in test-first order with dependency edges; AC coverage verified at
  100% (`proceed`).
- 2026-10-12T11:31Z — effort/risk recomputed against the 7-child WBS:
  effort Large (expected 65 h, recommended 89 h, range 54–144 h), risk High
  (score 14), confidence 88%; stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9` — Herdr plugin: activity-gated proxy mode switching

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Round 2 was asked interactively in the plan session (session id recorded in the
work-item comments); answers received 2026-10-12.

- **Q1:** Should we implement immediately, or investigate the fast/cheap ×

data.description:
Discovered during WL-0MV4V3WJN0013EZZ (discovered-from:WL-0MV4V3WJN0013EZZ).

## Problem

In the implement skill orchestrator, `phase_finish()` handles a non-fast-forward push to dev by attempting a rebase-and-retry, but the retry path references an undefined local `cwd`:

```
ERROR: Unhandled exception: name 'cwd' is not defined
```

File: `implement.py` (phase_finish, `PushNonFastForwardError` handler). The function's working-directory variable is named `worktree_path`/`repo_root`, not `cwd`.

## Impact

When dev advances concurrently (a sibling work item pushes first), `implement.py finish` crashes after commit + worktree removal instead of rebasing and retrying the push. The work item is reset to open and recovery must be done manually.

## Reproduction

1. Start a worktree from dev.
2. Let another commit land on origin/dev.
3. Run `implement.py finish` — the main-checkout fast-forward fails, the direct push is rejected non-fast-forward, and the retry rebase crashes with NameError.

## Expected

The retry path should rebase the feature branch onto origin/dev and retry the push (or report an actionable error), not raise NameError.

## Evidence

Observed 2026-10-12 during WL-0MV4V3WJN0013EZZ; commit c34af4d0 was rebased manually onto a415463d and pushed as 1c34755b.

# Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Lock the cross-package, versioned on-disk contract for the model-cooldown
marker **before** any behaviour slice, so the TUI writer and the herdr reader
cannot drift (parent constraint: the on-disk signal format is a cross-package
contract and must be versioned/tolerant, with unknown fields ignored).

## Target outcome

One shared module (the same pattern as the existing
`@worklog/shared/lease-release`) provides the contract and the tolerant
reader/writer used by both packages:

- `resolveMachineCoordinationDir()` — `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR` override (with
  `~` expansion) else `~/.herdr/downtime`; `null` when unresolvable.
- `readModelCooldowns(dir, now)` — active entries only (`cooldownUntil` in the
  future); tolerant (unknown fields ignored, malformed entries skipped); `[]`
  for a missing file; fails closed when the file is unreadable/corrupt.
- `writeModelCooldown(dir, entry)` — atomic (temp file + rename) upsert keyed by
  `paneId`/`sessionId`, pruning expired entries.
- `clearModelCooldown(dir, key)` — remove one entry; a missing file is a no-op.

Record shape (versioned; unknown fields ignored by readers):

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "cooldowns": [
    {
      "paneId": "<herdr pane id>",
      "sessionId": "<pi session id>",
      "itemId": "WL-... or null",
      "kind": "plan|intake|implement|audit|risk-effort or null",
      "reason": "all providers exhausted",
      "createdAt": 1700000000000,
      "cooldownUntil": 1700000300000
    }
  ]
}
```

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first for the five behaviours below (round trip, tolerance, malformed
   entry, expiry prune, missing vs unreadable, dir resolution).
2. The shared module implementing the functions and owning the field semantics
   (its header comment is the contract of record).
3. Export the subpath from the shared package manifest.
4. Make the herdr `getMachineCoordinationDir()` delegate to the shared resolver
   so there is a single source of truth (its existing tests must stay green).
5. No behaviour change in the herdr or TUI packages in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A durable, versioned, machine-readable cooldown contract exists with `schemaVersion` and tolerant readers (unknown fields ignored) in the shared package, importable by both the TUI recovery loop and herdr.
- [ ] A write-read-clear round-trip test proves a record with cooldownUntil and its pane/session key is written, read back and cleared.
- [ ] Tolerant reads: malformed entries are skipped and unknown fields are ignored without throwing, verified by tests.
- [ ] Expiry: entries with cooldownUntil in the past are not active and are pruned on the next write, verified by tests.
- [ ] Fail-closed reads: a missing or corrupt file is distinguished, verified by tests.
- [ ] Memory: the herdr coordination-dir resolver delegates to the shared one and its existing tests pass.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (the AC extraction used by planning tooling reads only
the first line of each bullet, so the full wording lives here).

- AC1 elaborates parent AC1 ("Durable cooldown record"): the record is durable
  (on disk, machine-wide) and machine-readable; it carries `paneId`/`sessionId`
  as the key plus `itemId`, `kind`, `reason`, `createdAt`, `cooldownUntil`.
- AC2: writer then reader then clearer, asserting the entry disappears.
- AC3: `{"schemaVersion": 1, "cooldowns": [{"paneId": "p"}]}` (missing fields)
  and `{"cooldowns": "not-an-array"}` must not throw.
- AC4: a past `cooldownUntil` is filtered out of `readModelCooldowns` and
  removed by the next `writeModelCooldown`.
- AC5: `null`/absent dir, a non-JSON file, and an unreadable file each resolve
  deterministically.
- AC6: `HERDR_COORDINATION_DIR`, `~/`-prefixed values, and the `~/.herdr/downtime`
  default are asserted through the shared resolver.

## Deliverables

- The shared cooldown-contract module and its unit tests.
- The subpath export in the shared package manifest.
- The herdr coordination-dir resolver delegating to the shared resolver, with
  its existing tests still green.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.test.ts`
- `packages/shared/package.json`
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/machine-coordination.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None. Created first: the contract/verification slice (test-first ordering) and a
prerequisite for every behaviour slice below.

# Recovery loop records durable cooldown

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

When the in-pane recovery loop classifies a model-unavailable error as
`SERVER_ERROR` (exhaustion patterns: "all providers exhausted", "all providers
unavailable", "no provider is available during the current scheduled time
window") and starts a backoff, write a durable machine-wide cooldown marker;
clear it on the next successful provider response. Today that state lives only
in in-memory `RetryState`.

## Target outcome

- Exhaustion `SERVER_ERROR` → write a marker with
  `cooldownUntil = now + delayMs` via the shared contract from the contract
  slice.
- The next 2xx observed by `createRetryHintCapturingFetch` → clear the marker.
- `itemId`/`kind` derived best-effort from `ctx.sessionManager.getEntries()`
  (first user message carrying a work-item id and a dispatch-kind token); left
  `null` when not derivable — the dispatcher then resolves them from the pane
  label. The marker key is always `paneId` (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) + `sessionId`.
- Best-effort: an unwritable or unreadable marker never throws and never aborts
  the retry loop.

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first: write on exhaustion `SERVER_ERROR` using the resolved delay; no
   write for a non-exhaustion retryable error; clear on 2xx; id/kind derivation
   present and absent; missing `HERDR_PANE_ID` degrades to a session-only key;
   an unwritable directory does not throw.
2. Expose `cooldownUntil` (`now + delayMs`) from `resolveRetryDelay()` without
   changing the existing `delayMs`/`serverHintMs` results.
3. Call the writer from the `SERVER_ERROR` branch of `register-recovery.ts` and
   the clearer from the existing 2xx path of `installFetchRetryHintCapture()`.
4. Keep the notify/stale-ctx safety contract intact (no new throwing paths).
5. Update the source comments describing the retry loop's side effects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Durable cooldown record: when a pane's recovery loop starts a backoff, a durable record with cooldownUntil is written and cleared on success.
- [ ] Detection: an exhaustion SERVER_ERROR writes the marker and a plain retryable 5xx or timeout does not, verified by tests.
- [ ] Item identity: itemId and kind are derived from session entries when present and left null when absent, with the pane/session key always written.
- [ ] Best-effort: an unwritable or unreadable marker never throws and never aborts the retry loop, verified by tests.
- [ ] Constraint: no slot-count completion gate, no dispatch pause and no unbounded latch are introduced.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC1 (parent AC1 "Durable cooldown record"): the record is written with
  `cooldownUntil = now + delayMs` for the current retry, carrying item id, kind,
  reason and the pane/session key, and is removed when the next provider
  response is 2xx (the same signal that currently clears the retry hint).
- Detection: reuse the existing `ErrorCategory.SERVER_ERROR` classification —
  no new pattern matching; assert the exhaustion bodies listed above and
  assert a plain 500/`TIMEOUT` writes nothing.
- Item identity: session entries are scanned for a work-item id token and a
  dispatch kind; on a miss the key is pane/session only and `itemId`/`kind` are
  null.
- Best-effort: point the writer at an unwritable directory (or a read-only dir)
  and assert the retry loop still resolves.

## Deliverables

- The recovery-loop writer/clearer wiring and its tests.
- `cooldownUntil` exposed from `resolveRetryDelay()` without changing existing
  results.
- Updated source comments describing the new side effects.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-loop.test.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`

## Dependencies

Depends on `Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader`.

# Cheap-switch gate honours model cooldowns

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

The herdr mode-switch worker must not switch the machine-wide proxy to `cheap`
while any active model-cooldown exists. A pane sitting in proxy backoff holds no
slot, so the proxy looks idle and the leader currently flips the shared proxy to
cheap — adding concurrency (cheap has more slots than fast) during a known
provider-exhaustion window.

## Target outcome

- `mode-switch-worker.tick()` reads the shared cooldown signal (the same
  pattern as `readSharedActivity`) and holds **fast** while any `cooldownUntil`
  is in the future.
- The hold is bounded by `cooldownUntil`: no latch, no persisted state — the
  first tick after expiry performs the normal idle/cheap decision.
- The fast-on-command path (`onOperatorCommand`) is unaffected.
- Reach is machine-wide: a cooldown written for any worklog root suppresses the
  shared-proxy cheap switch (the coordination dir is machine-wide, not per-root).

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first in the mode-switch worker test file: cooldown present → no cheap
   POST; expired → cheap POST; absent → cheap POST; unreadable/corrupt →
   fail-closed (no cheap POST); fast path still POSTs `fast` while a cooldown is
   active.
2. Read the cooldown signal in `tick()` before the mode read and return early
   when any entry is active; keep the coordination dir injectable for tests.
3. Cross-root integration test: a marker written for one root suppresses the
   switch when the worker is configured for another root (one machine-wide
   coordination dir, two roots).
4. Update the mode-switch design doc in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC2 — Cheap-switch gate: while at least one active model-cooldown exists, tick does not POST cheap; the hold is bounded by cooldownUntil.
- [ ] AC4 — Cross-root gate: a cooldown recorded in any worklog root suppresses the cheap switch.
- [ ] Fast path: onOperatorCommand still POSTs fast while a cooldown is active, verified by a test.
- [ ] No latch: the first tick at or after cooldownUntil performs the normal cheap decision, verified by a test.
- [ ] Fail-closed: an unreadable or corrupt signal produces no cheap POST, verified by a test.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC2 (parent AC2 "Cheap-switch gate"): the four-unit-test matrix is cooldown
  present / expired / absent / unreadable, each asserting the cheap POST or its
  absence, plus an assertion that the fast-on-command path is untouched.
- AC4 (parent AC4 "Cross-root gate"): write the marker through the shared store
  for root A, construct the worker for root B, assert no cheap POST; this is the
  integration test spanning two roots.
- No latch: after expiry the tick performs `GET /admin/mode` and the normal
  switch decision exactly as before the change.
- Fail-closed direction: "no cheap switch" is the safe direction (the proxy
  stays fast); the condition is logged so it is not silent.
- The withdrawn client drain must not return: no slot-count completion gate, no
  dispatch pause, no unbounded latch in the gate path.

## Deliverables

- The mode-switch gate change plus its unit tests.
- The cross-root integration test.
- The updated mode-switch design document.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`
- `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`

## Dependencies

Depends on `Cooldown signal contract and tolerant reader`.

# Bounded wake of one cooled-down job

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

At or after `cooldownUntil`, resume **at most one** model-cooldown job through
the existing stalled-resume path (literal `continue` to a live pane, or a
relaunch of pi `--continue` in an exited pane) rather than waiting for the
generic stall threshold or opening a brand-new pane.

## Target outcome

- The dispatcher consults the shared cooldown signal and, when at least one
  entry has expired, feeds that candidate into the existing stalled-resume
  machinery — at most one resume per cycle.
- The existing safety gates still apply: the non-terminal pane-close cooldown,
  the per-item/per-kind attempt cap, and the `needsProducerReview` exclusion.
- A successful resume consumes/clears the marker so the same pane is not woken
  repeatedly; a failed resume stays bounded by `cooldownUntil` and the attempt
  cap.

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first in the stalled-work and downtime-worker dispatch test files:
   expired cooldown yields a candidate; unexpired cooldown does not; at most one
   resume per cycle; the attempt cap and `needsProducerReview` still exclude a
   cooldown candidate; a successful resume consumes the marker.
2. Add an expired-cooldown candidate source in `stalled-work.ts` (mapping
   `paneId` to the pane record the scan already reads) or extend
   `classifyStalledPane` with the cooldown input.
3. Wire it into the dispatcher's pre-dispatch stalled scan seam so at most one
   cooldown resume happens per cycle, preferring it over opening a new pane.
4. Ensure the wake uses the unchanged `STALLED_RESUME_PROMPT` and the existing
   attempt accounting.
5. Update the downtime-dispatcher doc in this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC3 — Bounded wake: at/after cooldownUntil the dispatcher resumes at most one job via the stalled-resume path.
- [ ] Strictness: an unexpired cooldown never wakes a pane, verified by tests.
- [ ] Safety gates: a cooldown candidate is still excluded by the attempt cap and by the needsProducerReview flag, verified by tests.
- [ ] Bounded concurrency: at most one cooldown resume per dispatcher cycle, verified by tests.
- [ ] Consumption: a successful resume consumes the marker so it is not re-woken on the next cycle; a failed resume remains bounded, verified by tests.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC3 (parent AC3 "Bounded wake"): reuse `classifyStalledPane` /
  `resumeStalledPane` — the literal `continue` prompt to a live pane and the pi
  `--continue` relaunch for an exited pane both stay the only wake mechanisms;
  the attempt-cap and `needsProducerReview` exclusions are asserted against a
  cooldown-sourced candidate.
- Strictness: `cooldownUntil` in the future must not produce a wake even when
  the generic stall threshold has elapsed.
- Bounded concurrency: the cycle reports `{ ok: true, stalledResume: true }` on
  one resume and must not offer new work in the same cycle.
- Failed resume: a neutral failure reason is not turned into a CLI-error strike,
  a crash or a duplicate resume.

## Deliverables

- The expired-cooldown candidate source and the dispatcher wiring.
- The stalled-work and dispatcher test coverage.
- The updated downtime-dispatcher developer document.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/stalled-work.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/stalled-work.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

Depends on `Cheap-switch gate honours model cooldowns`.

# Bounded default cooldown and fail-closed hardening

**Parent:** WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9 (Resume model-exhausted jobs instead of switching to cheap)

## Goal

Make the cooldown best-effort but never unbounded, and keep every failure path
fail-closed: an absent or unparseable `Retry-After` yields a bounded default
cooldown, and an unreadable signal never causes a premature cheap switch.

## Target outcome

- A bounded default cooldown (with a documented clamp floor and ceiling) is used
  when the recovery loop has no usable server hint.
- An absent or malformed `Retry-After` yields that bounded default — never an
  unbounded hold and never a zero hold.
- A truthful long hint stays clamped by the existing server-hint ceiling
  (6 hours), so no unbounded hold is possible.
- The gate distinguishes an absent/empty signal (normal cheap decision) from an
  unreadable/corrupt signal (hold fast, log the condition).
- Stale markers left by a crashed pane expire by `cooldownUntil` and are pruned
  on write.

## Minimal implementation

1. Tests first in the recovery settings and retry-logic test files: no hint →
   bounded default; malformed hint → bounded default; an over-ceiling honest
   hint is clamped.
2. Add the bounded default (and its clamp) to the recovery config defaults in
   `DEFAULT_RECOVERY_CONFIG`, documented alongside the existing
   `baseDelayMs`/`maxDelayMs` per-category values.
3. Sharpen the shared reader so absent, empty, unreadable and corrupt are
   distinguishable by callers.
4. Mode-switch gate tests: unreadable/corrupt → no cheap POST and a log; absent
   → the normal cheap decision.
5. Settings/pruning tests: a stale marker expires and is pruned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC5 — Fail-closed and bounded default: an unreadable/absent signal never switches cheap early; an absent Retry-After yields a bounded default cooldown.
- [ ] Bounded default: a documented default with a clamp floor and ceiling exists in the recovery configuration, verified by settings tests.
- [ ] Clamped ceiling: an honest server hint above the ceiling is clamped rather than honoured unbounded, verified by tests.
- [ ] Absent vs unreadable: an absent/empty signal permits the normal cheap decision while an unreadable/corrupt signal holds fast and is logged, verified by tests.
- [ ] Staleness: a marker from a crashed pane expires by cooldownUntil and is pruned on the next write, verified by tests.

## Verification detail

Elaborates the ACs above (planning tooling extracts only the first line of each
bullet).

- AC5 (parent AC5 "Fail-closed and bounded default"): "fail-closed" here means
  the proxy stays fast (no cheap POST) — never a premature cheap switch; the
  bounded default prevents an unbounded hold when the server gives no hint.
- Bounded default home: the retry loop (which owns the cooldown computation)
  lives in the TUI extension, so the default belongs in the recovery
  configuration rather than the herdr settings schema; the herdr side only
  reads the resulting signal.
- Clamped ceiling: reuse the existing `serverHintMaxDelayMs` (6 h) so a
  truthful long `Retry-After` keeps working (WL-0MUR5EGH7003VOHM) while a
  malformed or absurd value cannot pin the cooldown open.
- Staleness: the writer prunes expired entries; the reader never reports an
  expired entry as active.

## Deliverables

- The bounded default cooldown (with clamp) in the recovery configuration.
- The clamped-ceiling and absent-vs-unreadable behaviour and their tests.
- The stale-marker expiry/prune tests.
- The updated README settings documentation.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/error-patterns.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/settings.test.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-logic.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-after.test.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/README.md`

## Dependencies

Depends on `Recovery loop records durable cooldown`.

discovered-from:WL-0MV4V6LJQ0050FZX

In the global implement skill (~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py), phase_finish's non-fast-forward push recovery path calls run_cmd(['git', 'rebase', 'origin/dev'], cwd=cwd) where cwd is undefined (the function scope uses worktree_path). This raises 'name cwd is not defined', aborts the finish, and resets the work item to open after the commit/build/test steps, leaving the push unperformed.

Repro: a concurrent push advances origin/dev between the local commit and the push; the push fails non-fast-forward; the recovery path is entered.

Workaround used: manually rebase the feature branch onto local dev and push <branch>:refs/heads/dev.

Suggested fix: reference the in-scope worktree path variable (worktree_path) in the rebase/retry block. The skill is external to this repo; fix belongs in the framework source.

# Downtime dispatcher: prefer audit-tier items in cheap windows

discovered-from:WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5

## Problem statement

The mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` spawn env
(WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME) is set only for an **audit-tier** downtime dispatch in
**cheap** mode with a genuinely free second slot and single-flight dispatch
(`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions()` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).

In practice the downtime dispatcher almost never selects an audit-tier item
during a cheap window, so the mode-aware path is unreachable and its benefit
is unmeasurable at runtime. The measurement item **WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5** has
been blocked on a runtime capture since 2026-09-25 for exactly this reason:
the retained `downtime-dispatches.log` contains only two unique audit
dispatches ever, and the single post-fix cheap-window one (2026-10-09) did not
reach Phase 2.

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants the mode-aware parallelism change to be
  exercised so it can be validated and its cheap-slot benefit confirmed.

User story:

- *As the operator, I want the downtime dispatcher to prefer audit-tier work
  items during cheap windows, so the mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`

Implement `watchDbChanges` in `packages/herdr/src/db-change.ts` (parent WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN).

## Goal
A cheap, cross-process-safe watch over the worklog change signal so the pane can react to an agent write promptly.

## Scope
- `watchDbChanges(cacheDir, worklogDir, opts)`: watches the state-counter file (`state/<hash>.json`) and/or `worklog.db`/`-wal`, debounces/coalesces bursts, and emits a change callback.
- Fail open: any watch/read error is reported as unavailable so the caller falls back to polling. Never throws into the TUI loop.
- `dispose()`/`close()` for teardown on pane exit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `watchDbChanges` watches the cross-process DB-change signal (state counter and/or SQLite `worklog.db`/`-wal`), debounces events, and emits at most one change callback per burst.
- The watch fails open: any read or `fs.watch` error is reported as unavailable and the caller falls back to the 30 s auto-refresh tick.
- Watch teardown (`dispose`) removes all `fs.watch` handles and timers.
- Unit tests cover the watch trigger, debounce/coalescing, and fail-open fallback, with injected `fs.watch`/clock.

## Implementation notes
- Prefer `node:fs` `watch` (no new runtime dependencies). Handle the state-counter file being absent at start-up (watch the `state/` directory or fall back to polling).
- Inject `fs.watch`/timers for deterministic tests (mirror the `db-change.test.ts` mocking style).

- F1 verification harness (shared contract tests).

data.description:
# implement.py finish crashes in the non-fast-forward rebase-retry path

**Discovered from:** WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ

## Problem

When `implement.py finish` commits successfully but `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev`
is rejected as non-fast-forward (dev advanced concurrently), the recovery
path raises an unhandled exception:

```
ERROR: Unhandled exception: name 'cwd' is not defined
```

## Location

Global implement skill (not tracked in this repo):
`~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py`, in the
`PushNonFastForwardError` handler (~line 4305):

```python
rebase_result = run_cmd(
    ["git", "rebase", "origin/dev"],
    cwd=cwd,          # <-- NameError: 'cwd' is not defined in this scope
)
```

The surrounding function has `repo_root`, `branch`, `worktree_path` — no `cwd`.

## Impact

- The finish phase has ALREADY committed and removed the worktree by this point,
  so the agent is left with: work committed on the local feature branch, the
  worktree deleted, status reset to `open`, and nothing pushed.
- Requires manual recovery (fetch, re-create worktree for the branch, rebase onto
  `origin/dev`, push).
- Secondary issue: the retry pushes from `repo_root` (main checkout) and the
  rebase (if it ran) would target the checked-out branch, not the feature
  branch — the rebase should run against the feature branch before worktree
  removal, or use an explicit ref.

## Reproduction

1. Start an implementation; let it commit.
2. Push `dev` from another actor between the worktree fork and the finish push
   so the finish push is rejected non-fast-forward.
3. `implement.py finish` raises `name 'cwd' is not defined` after committing and
   removing the worktree.

## Observed in

WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ (cheap-switch gate): finish committed `180b9775`, removed the
worktree, then crashed; recovered by rebasing the branch onto `origin/dev` and
pushing (`a6f5ca98`).

In a multi-agent repo, another agent's implement.py finish fast-forwards the main checkout's refs/heads/dev and creates/removes its own agent worktree; the guard attributes these to the tested suite and sets success=False (live_repo_mutation), blocking implement.py finish and test verification even though every test passed.

data.description:
Discovered during WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6 (discovered-from:WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6).

## Problem
`implement.py finish`'s test gate failed twice with a spurious 'live-repo mutation detected' verdict even though the canonical suite passed (both declared commands exited 0). The guard (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` `snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`, used by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`) snapshots refs, local `.git/config`, registered worktrees, and `git status` before/after the suite. On a multi-agent host with several active worktrees, concurrent agent activity moved:
- `refs/remotes/origin/dev` (observed bbc8e89a -> 4163175)
- `refs/heads/dev` (main checkout's local dev, advanced by another agent's finish fast-forward)
- another agent's feature branch ref

Only refs checked out in agent worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/` (and their `branch.<name>.*` config) are excluded, so these deltas fail the gate.

## Impact
`implement.py finish` fails after a ~17-minute suite run and resets the item to `open`; the agent must sync its worktree to the latest `dev` and re-warm the test cache before retrying. Observed twice on WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6.

## Possible fix
Exclude `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/*` (or ignore ref movement entirely) from the mutation diff while still catching working-tree mutations caused by the suite itself; or scope the ref check to refs the suite could plausibly touch.

## Workaround
Fast-forward the worktree to the latest `origin/dev`, run the full suite once to warm the per-command cache, then re-run `implement.py finish` (cache hits shrink the race window).

## Clarifying questions for drag-to-scroll intake

The current description has placeholder acceptance criteria. To draft a proper intake brief, I need clarification on the following:

**Q1: Scope of drag-to-scroll**
Drag-to-scroll should work in which areas?
- (a) List area only — scrolling the work item list up/down as you drag (most common)
- (b) Detail view only — scrolling the document content
- (c) Both list and detail areas
- (d) List, detail, and metadata panel

**Q2: Drag detection threshold**
How should we distinguish a drag-to-scroll gesture from other drag motions (hover tooltip trigger)?
- (a) Any drag motion (>0 pixels movement) initiates scroll
- (b) A minimum distance threshold (e.g., 3–5 pixel movement) before scroll starts
- (c) Distinguish by speed: slow/small = hover, fast/large = scroll

**Q3: Scroll behaviour**
- (a) Proportional to drag distance (1 pixel drag = proportional scroll in list area)
- (b) Snap-to-row — each row boundary crossed advances/retreats the scroll offset by one row
- (c) Hybrid: proportional within the visible area, snapping at row boundaries

**Q4: Touch drag vs click-drag**
Should touch-drag and click-drag behave identically, or differently?
- (a) Identical behaviour for both
- (b) Touch-drag = continuous scroll; click-drag = click-drag-select (toggle off mouse first)

**Q5: Interaction with hover tooltip**
Currently, drag-motion events (button & 32) trigger hover tooltips in list mode.
- (a) Replace hover tooltip entirely with drag-to-scroll
- (b) Coexist: hover on small/slow drags, scroll on large/fast drags
- (c) Hover only on mouse motion (no button pressed); scroll on button+motion

Please respond with your preferences (e.g., "1c, 2b, 3a, 4a, 5a"). If unsure, my recommendation is: 1a, 2b (3px threshold), 3a (proportional), 4a (identical), 5c (hover only without button).,

data.comment:
## Appendix: answers to clarifying questions

- **Q1 (scope of drag-to-scroll):** Answer (operator): **c — both list and detail areas**. Source: interactive reply 2026-10-12.
- **Q2 (drag detection threshold):** Answer (operator): "your call". Final: **(b) minimum distance threshold of 3 pixels** — a small dead-zone avoids misclassifying incidental pointer jitter during a click/double-click as a scroll, while still feeling immediate. Threshold is defined as a named constant so it can be tuned. Source: operator delegated; agent recommendation.
- **Q3 (scroll behaviour):** Answer (operator): "your call". Final: **(a) proportional to drag distance, snapped to row boundaries** — drag accumulates a fractional row offset; the integer part advances/retreats the list scroll offset so content tracks the finger/pointer, with each whole row crossing producing a discrete row step. For the detail view, drag maps proportionally to line offsets (1 row ≈ 1 line) with the same integer accumulation. Source: operator delegated; agent recommendation.
- **Q4 (touch drag vs click-drag):** Answer (operator): **a — identical behaviour for both**. Source: interactive reply 2026-10-12.
- **Q5 (hover tooltip interaction):** Answer (operator): "your call". Final: **(c) hover only on button-less motion; scroll on button-held motion** — SGR motion events carry the button state, so motion with the left button held (button 0 + 32 motion bit) becomes drag-to-scroll, while button-less motion (button 35 = 3 + 32 motion bit, i.e. no button held) continues to drive the hover tooltip. This preserves the existing tooltip behaviour (WL-0MT9XRZDK006GMUH) without conflating it with dragging. Source: operator delegated; agent recommendation.

Research notes: inspected `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — motion events are currently handled at `mapMouseToAction` (button & 32 branch returns `hover-row`/`hover-none`); the SGR parser (`parseMouseEvent`) already exposes the button number, so the held-button state is available. The list state class exposes `scrollOffset` (integer rows) and the detail view uses a line-based `detailScrollOffset`; both are already driven by wheel/keyboard paths that a drag handler can reuse.

**This supersedes the earlier comment of this session ("mechanism still
unexercised").** That comment was based on a scan of only the *archived*
daily report subdirectories and only the ContextHub dispatch log. The
proxy-usage archive **lags by up to ~2 days**, so the most recent window was
not yet in any `YYYY-MM-DD/` subdirectory — only in the **live root**
`~/proxy-usage-reports/cheap_sessions.csv` / `fast_sessions.csv`. Checking the
root report (window 2026-10-11 05:00 → 2026-10-12 05:00) and the dispatch logs
of **all** repos reveals the capture the item was waiting for.

### The capture: 2026-10-11 cheap window (post runner-fix)

Two **dispatched** epic audits ran their Phase 2 child fan-out in the
01:00-10:00 local cheap window on **2026-10-11**, with genuine overlap:

| Epic (dispatched) | Dispatch (UTC) | Mode | Cheap `phase2_child` sessions | Peak concurrency | Fan-out span | Σ child durations | Speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AH-0MV2SGIX5005PFJT` (AI_Hell) | 2026-10-11T01:13Z | cheap | 6 | **2** | 2858 s | 5318 s | **1.86** |
| `MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY` (tce-main-street) | 2026-10-11T02:02Z & 04:18Z | cheap | 6 (of 9) | **2** | 2945 s | 5517 s | **1.87** |

Both were dispatched by the downtime worker into the cheap window; both ran
`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2`, so their Phase 2 children ran **two at a time**
(e.g. `MS-0MV16VXDZ007NBK8` 09:18:13-09:39:36 overlapping
`MS-0MV16VX310089U2L` 09:18:30-09:32:05; `AH-0MV2XDD65009WTJ4` 08:55:28-09:03:50
overlapping `AH-0MV2X4RFZ006JGQG` 08:55:52-09:04:26). The two epics ran
concurrently, so the combined cheap-mode peak across the proxy was 4 — which
is also why remote fallback must be checked as a guardrail (below).

**This is the mechanism firing**: `_resolve_child_concurrency()` with a
`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)` produces exactly this pairwise overlap;
`max_workers=1` (the old cheap-mode serialisation, pre-fix) is strictly
sequential and peaks at 1.

data.comment:
## Diagnosis (WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G)

The previous fix (48dd9d06) only changed the `sortedAll` order in `src/commands/list.ts`. Two real defects remained, which explains 'no difference':

1. **Concise/tree renderer discarded the computed order.** `displayItemTreeWithFormat` (used by `wl list -F concise` / the config-short human display) re-sorts its input by database position (`sortIndex`), silently throwing away the 6-bucket order `list.ts` had just computed. A list created medium→high→low rendered medium→high→low (the exact symptom). Fixed by threading a `preserveOrder` flag and passing `isInReviewList`.

2. **The herdr TUI dropped audit fingerprint metadata.** `regroupWorkItems` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` built its sort comparator without `fingerprint`/`currentFingerprint`, so `inReviewBucket` fell back to the 60s time gate. A passed-audit item that is fresh by the primary content gate but time-stale was classified `passed-stale` (bucket 5) instead of `passed-fresh` (bucket 6), ranking it ahead of a higher-priority `passed-fresh` item — i.e. 'medium before high'. `fetchNextItems` also lost fingerprints because `wl next` does not emit them and dedup kept the `wl next` copy; `fetchNextItems` now enriches from the mandatory `wl list` subset. This makes the default worklist and the stage-filtered view classify buckets identically (AC2/AC4).

The within-bucket priority comparator itself was verified correct (fuzz-tested over 5000 random in_review sets) and unchanged.

### Fix summary
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`: forward `fingerprint`/`currentFingerprint` through `regroupWorkItems`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`: enrich `fetchNextItems` items with audit metadata from the mandatory `wl list` subset.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` + `src/commands/list.ts`: preserve the computed in_review order in the concise/tree renderer.
- Tests: `grouping.test.ts`, new `fetcher-in-review-bucket.test.ts`, new `list-in-review-concise-order.test.ts`, `helpers-tree-rendering.test.ts`.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Re-implementation after producer rejection (priority-first sort)

**Root cause of the rejection.** Within the In Review section the audit bucket was the *primary* sort key and priority only the secondary key. A medium-priority item with a failed audit (bucket 2/3) therefore ranked ahead of a high-priority item with no audit (bucket 4) — exactly the medium-before-high order the producer reported. The previous fix (a415463d) only corrected fingerprint propagation and the concise renderer; it did not change the key precedence, so the symptom persisted.

**Fix.** `compareInReviewItems` (both `src/commands/grouping.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`, kept in lockstep) now sorts by:
1. priority (high → medium → low) — primary
2. audit bucket (needsProducerReview → failed-fresh → failed-stale → no-audit → passed-stale → passed-fresh) — secondary, within a priority band
3. updatedAt (older first), then id — deterministic tie-breakers

Because `compareGroupableItems`, `regroupWorkItems`, `list.ts` and both fetcher paths all delegate to `compareInReviewItems`, the change applies to the default worklist, the stage-filtered view, and `wl list --stage in_review`.

**Tests.** Added cross-priority regressions to `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-in-review-bucket.test.ts`, `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` and an end-to-end CLI case in `tests/cli/list-in-review-concise-order.test.ts`. The prior test that asserted bucket-over-priority ordering was updated to the refined priority-first contract. Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md`.

data.comment:
Gap detected in the prior implementation (commit 55d8db90, already on dev) — AC1 was unmet.

**Evidence:** running `bash packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh` left a reparented `sleep infinity` (PPID 1) after completion (observed PIDs 37067, 41271, 42053). AC2/AC3 passed only because the earlier fix redirected the wrapper's stdout/stderr to /dev/null; the grandchild process still leaked.

**Root cause:** the first test case killed only the wrapper leader (`kill "$PID"`) and then cleared `TEST_PIDS=()`, so the EXIT-trap never reached the wrapper's process group where `sleep infinity` lives.

**Fix (this commit):** kill the wrapper's whole process group (`set -m` makes PGID == PID), keep the entry tracked so the EXIT trap force-kills any survivor, trap INT/TERM so an external `timeout` also triggers cleanup, and add an explicit regression assertion that the group is empty after the kill.

**Verified:** AC1 no orphaned process (new assertion passes); AC2 piped invocation 3s (<30s); AC3 `timeout 10` completes in 2s; TERM-mid-run leaves no orphans; existing assertions unchanged (18 passed, 0 failed).

- index.ts: production wiring via createProductionHydratorDeps().listTabs + HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID.
- Tests: hydrator.test.ts (pure helper + fail-open + workspace scoping) and new worklist-active-tab-marker.test.ts (marker shown/hidden/scope).

The ship release process owns and regenerates it, so a manual entry here would conflict with the generator.

**Evidence the change will be recorded automatically:**
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` queries `wl list --stage in_review` and includes **parent-level** items only (`getParentsOnly`: `parentId === null`).

- `merge-dev-to-main.sh` runs the generator and commits `CHANGELOG.md` only on an actual release.

**Test-count/runtime impact:** recorded durably in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (post-change section) and on WL-0MV4V0IF9008214R, rather than in the player-facing CHANGELOG (whose entries are LLM-generated, player-focused descriptions, not developer metrics).

**Acceptance criteria mapping:**
- 'The change is recorded in the CHANGELOG' → satisfied at release by the pipeline (not feasible manually without fighting the generator).
- 'Follows the existing CHANGELOG format' → guaranteed by the generator.
- 'Notes the test-count/runtime impact' → recorded in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`; the player-facing CHANGELOG intentionally omits developer metrics.

data.comment:
Implementation summary (WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ)

**Change:** Added a machine-wide model-cooldown gate to `mode-switch-worker.tick()`. After the leader/proxy-idle gates and before `GET /admin/mode`, the worker reads `readModelCooldowns(coordinationDir, now())` (shared contract WL-0MV563825002R9Y1). While any entry has `cooldownUntil > now` it returns early, holding the proxy fast; the reader returns only active entries, so the hold is bounded by `cooldownUntil` with no latch.

**Decisions/assumptions:**
- Fail-closed: a `null` reader result (unreadable/corrupt signal, unresolvable dir) holds fast and logs the hold. A *missing* file is `[]` (nothing recorded) and does not suppress the switch.
- The gate is skipped when `coordinationDir` is `undefined` (legacy/test default). Production always passes a dir (`index.ts`: `getMachineCoordinationDir() ?? join(targetCwd, '.worklog')`), so production still fail-closes; gating on a defined dir preserves the existing shared-activity/legacy tests.
- Fast path untouched: `onOperatorCommand` never reads the cooldown signal.
- No client drain reintroduced: no slot-count completion gate, no dispatch pause, no unbounded latch.

**Tests:** unit matrix in `mode-switch-worker.test.ts` (active -> hold, expired -> cheap, absent -> cheap, unreadable/corrupt -> fail-closed, no-latch expiry -> cheap, fast-on-command -> fast) and a cross-root integration test in `mode-switch-integration.test.ts` (one machine dir, two roots; a marker for root A suppresses root B's switch, and clearing it resumes the switch). Docs updated in `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`.

**Verification:** herdr typecheck clean; `npm run build` clean; 22 test files / 619 tests pass (mode-switch-worker, mode-switch-integration, tests/herdr).

data.comment:
Manual verification note (WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) — cold default-view refresh.

Benchmark: `npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (1000 root items, 20 expanded parents x 3 children, 2 iterations). Run as an A/B against the same harness at HEAD (5ff1372d) under identical machine load (load average ~45-48 on 16 cores), alternating runs:

- baseline (before): cold 4931 / 5663 / 2329 ms, 25 `wl` spawns, withinTarget=false
- consolidated (after): cold 1402 / 502 / 1551 ms, 3 `wl` spawns, withinTarget=true

Spawn count 25 -> 3 (-88%): one `wl next` + two mandatory-subset `wl list` queries. The review-queue state is deduplicated against the mandatory in_review subset, and the actionable count plus expanded-children reads are served in-process from SQLite. Worst measured cold refresh on the loaded host was 1.55 s (<= 2 s target); the deterministic regression guard is the spawn count.

Semantics: the mandatory critical/in_review subsets stay on the `wl` spawn path so the CLI's git-based `currentFingerprint` audit-freshness enrichment is preserved exactly; the in-process children fast path falls back to `wl list --parent` whenever a matched child carries a stored audit fingerprint (audit dispatch is root-only, so this is rare). A fresh WorklogDatabase handle is opened and closed per read, so no stale cache can be served across a refresh.
